A mirrored red-and-blue tapestry narrows at its center, with two side diamonds, long red diagonal borders and small top and bottom chevrons. Red tiles are lethal until captured; blue tiles slow the player. Five pink ring bouncers begin in the upper center notch, upper-right field, right diagonal and two lower-left positions. Four cyan patrols start on the top and side rails. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.description: Recommended: Light carrier, then Heavy carrier. Reconnect both cartridge markers and reveal 68%. All classes can attempt an ordinary clear without this optional seal.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Open 85%. Horizontal and vertical warning lanes operate on different repeating schedules; watch the visible warnings and keep routing rather than waiting for a scripted opening. Fast field patrols, a contour scout and an awakening secured-ground rover pressure different parts of the board. Mud slows your craft; the marked hot zone is lethal while unrevealed. Optional freeze and life pickups reward a risky detour. A closed cut stops at safe ground; give a fresh direction to continue. Arcade: automatic contact pickups and a 15-cell-per-second cruise; no manual Scan, supply or Boost actions.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original revised fictional arcade routing layout; same original First Light picture reward, not an additional unique image or reference-game reconstruction.

Floating terraces surround the motif, with sparse archipelago along the lower route. 5 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 7 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Recommended: Fiber relay. Tactical challenge: reveal 48% and capture the northern relay. Cross Right through the signal band. Scan reveals information there, but is not required to win. On Standard, signal resistance preserves speed and equipment while the eight-second and 76-cell cable limits still apply. An ordinary craft can take the safe northern rim and cut beyond the band. Gentle removes those cut limits; it is separate relaxed practice.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original layout study with a distinct campaign identity and original scenic picture. Gameplay geometry is independent of scenery.
metadata.title: Signal Switchback

metadata.description: Red zigzag waves intersect three horizontal blue slowing bands, with additional red waves along the top and bottom. Four pink ring bouncers and one pink diamond eroder roam the field. Four cyan patrols start at the top, left and two right-side positions. Red tiles are lethal until captured; blue tiles slow your craft. Start at bottom center and close cuts on the safe perimeter to reveal 75%.

metadata.author: Reveal Line
metadata.description: Recommended: Light carrier, then Heavy carrier at the southern hangar. Refill at a supply pad and use a field to suppress an emitter before crossing. Restore both bridge relays and reveal 68%. Two supply/hangar stops and a 6.5-second cut budget reward a planned route. Other classes can take a slower ordinary line.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original fictional encounter adapted from the project Fieldcraft teaching layout.
metadata.title: River Switchyard

metadata.description: Red tiles form a ceramic ram silhouette with a large curled horn inspired by Opishne toys. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Open constellation surround the motif, with slalom gates along the lower route. 3 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 6 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Recommended: Fiber relay. Signal resistance keeps movement and equipment working through the band; your live cable can still break. Other classes can use the western and southern detour. Capture the visible shield objective first. The Mainframe warns horizontally, then after that objective warns vertically. Wait for the active stripe to end; during the opening close a cut with at least twelve new field cells. An early or short cut keeps ordinary gains but does not open the core. Missed openings repeat. If at most twelve field cells remain, wait safely outside a cut for an opening. This encounter has a shielded stage and an exposed stage.
metadata.rightsStatus: Exact Sentinel layout, independent theme owner and original scenic reward. Fictional setting; scenery does not define collision geometry.
metadata.title: The hilltop night transmission

metadata.description: Red tiles form five-petal periwinkle flowers on a curling branch. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Floating terraces surround the motif, with tidal coves along the lower route. 3 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 7 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

Red tiles form a handled ceramic pitcher with a floral ornament inspired by Kosiv. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Floating terraces surround the motif, with stepping stones along the lower route. 5 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 9 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Reveal 62%. The broken ring has four offset gates. Read the interceptor warning, then choose a northern or southern return; a wall cannot reconnect your line. The lower gate has a slow patch, while a speed pickup rewards the outer detour. Tap a direction to fly. A completed cut stops the craft; choose a fresh direction to continue.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original abstract geometry. Procedural FPV presentation; no new illustrations, stories or music.
metadata.title: Split Ring

metadata.description: Red pixel lettering spells UKRAINE. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Split riverbanks surround the motif, with broken crescents along the lower route. 4 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 5 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Open 65%. Two faster crossing patrols threaten your live line; the contour scout follows the changing reveal boundary. The central mud strip halves flight speed while it is covered. Detour for the speed pickup or choose a clear crossing. Closing a cut stops you: release held controls, then press a fresh direction. Boost with Shift; Pause remains available.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original revised fictional arcade routing layout; same original First Light picture reward, not an additional unique image or reference-game reconstruction.
metadata.title: Orchard Window

metadata.description: Red tiles form a long tapered Carpathian horn with a flared bell. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Offset garden courts surround the motif, with broken crescents along the lower route. 3 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 6 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Open 75%. Wall gaps leave broad crossings, but mud slows the direct route. Three fast field patrols share the field with an eroder: its warning marks one threatened secured cell. A rover wakes after its ground is revealed and a visible warning completes; newly opened space can become dangerous. Slow and freeze pickups offer exposed detours. Walls never close a cut. Reconnect, stop, then choose your next fresh direction.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original revised fictional arcade routing layout; same original First Light picture reward, not an additional unique image or reference-game reconstruction.
metadata.title: Split Courtyard

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Recommended: Scout. Tactical challenge: reveal 30%. Read the interceptor warning and choose either exit around the center barrier before closing at the bottom safe edge. Its locked target and travelling line-hit fronts make a stalled cable dangerous. Walls cannot close a cut. Manual equipment remains available; no supply charge is needed. This is an original route-choice study with fixed Standard grades, not a human-qualified difficulty rating.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original layout study with a distinct campaign identity and original scenic picture. Gameplay geometry is independent of scenery.
metadata.title: Split Signal Foundry

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Reveal 74%. The interceptor aims ahead of your visible heading, then keeps that target. Bait its warning and choose another exit. Wall gaps and mud make the direct crossing risky. A rover wakes on revealed ground; keep your return route clear. Tap a direction to fly; closing a cut stops the craft. Choose a fresh direction to continue.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original pressure layout. Existing owned First Light/Homeward Skies reward art; not new artwork or a reference-game copy.
metadata.title: Courtyard Exits

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: A square upper-left creative club and a long lower-right repair studio overlook roof gardens and a coral city sunset.
metadata.rightsStatus: Exact Countercurrent layout; independent theme owner and original scenery. Painted routes are not collision geometry.
metadata.title: After-Hours Rooftop Exchange

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Reveal 80%. Reveal a night canal and warm windows behind the crossfire. Watch the lane warning and keep a safe return path. The distant vehicles are illustration, not additional actors. Tap a direction to fly; closing a cut stops the craft. Choose a fresh direction to continue. Pressure Lines layout 3, presented as an original art variation.
metadata.rightsStatus: New original illustration over unchanged Pressure Lines gameplay. Distinct art and progress identity; not a new geometry or reference-game reconstruction.
metadata.title: Night Crossfire

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Four long warm-lit platform halls sit within a large sunset transit shed, with boxy CRTs near the balcony.
metadata.rightsStatus: Exact Countercurrent layout; independent theme owner and original scenery. Painted routes are not collision geometry.
metadata.title: Last Platforms of Summer

metadata.description: Recreate the supplied neon arena: seven blue slowing regions, six red lethal regions, two roaming pink orbs, a central diamond eroder and three cyan perimeter patrols. Capture 75%. Blue ground slows your craft; red ground is lethal until captured. The central revealed islands are safe return surfaces. Grid and starting positions are scaled from the picture; enemy behaviors and speeds are authored approximations.

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Open 85%. Horizontal and vertical warning lanes operate on different repeating schedules; watch the visible warnings and keep routing rather than waiting for a scripted opening. Fast field patrols, a contour scout and an awakening secured-ground rover pressure different parts of the board. Mud slows your craft; the marked hot zone is lethal while unrevealed. Optional freeze and life pickups reward a risky detour. A closed cut stops at safe ground; give a fresh direction to continue.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original revised fictional arcade routing layout; same original First Light picture reward, not an additional unique image or reference-game reconstruction.
metadata.title: Night Signal

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Reveal 74%. Reveal a sunlit rail-workshop courtyard through short, secured cuts. Two hunters commit to locked targets; choose another opening before they arrive. Tap a direction to fly; closing a cut stops the craft. Choose a fresh direction to continue. Pressure Lines layout 2, presented as an original art variation.
metadata.rightsStatus: New original illustration over unchanged Pressure Lines gameplay. Distinct art and progress identity; not a new geometry or reference-game reconstruction.
metadata.title: Courtyard Exits

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Recommended: Scout. Scan reveals the hidden cartridge and shows enemy direction hints; it does not slow enemies or capture territory. Reveal 45% and the cartridge. Read the two open courtyards before choosing the upper survey loop or lower outer approach. The center throat ends at a wall: walls cannot reconnect a cut. An enemy warns before committing to its target. A known route without Scan remains possible.
metadata.rightsStatus: Exact Sentinel layout, independent theme owner and original scenic reward. Fictional setting; scenery does not define collision geometry.
metadata.title: The radio-repair courtyard

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: Open 80% beneath the night signal. A horizontal warning lane flashes before its active sweep; cross during its quiet interval. Three field patrols and a faster perimeter scout keep cuts under pressure. The warning remains visible above the concealed picture. Pause anytime; only Resume restarts your flight.
metadata.rightsStatus: Original fictional arcade routing layout; not a reconstruction of an undocumented reference board.
metadata.title: Night Signal

metadata.author: RevealLine
metadata.description: A golden brick rotunda encloses record stalls and arcade cabinets around a tree and circular listening bench. Foreground crates, worn parquet, plain discs and open passages suggest a shared market before opening.
metadata.rightsStatus: Exact Fracture layout; independent theme owner and original scenery. Painted routes are not collision geometry.
metadata.title: The Record Market before Opening

metadata.description: Three tall cyan dividers and a double-width horizontal wall split eight red-and-blue switchback lanes. Broken cyan perimeter walls retain the screenshot openings. Red side rails and alternating crossbars flank blue slow terrain. Four yellow bouncers begin near the left outer lanes and on either side of the center wall at the far right. Two cyan patrols start along the bottom rail. Start at bottom center, move sideways to an opening, and reveal 75%.

Red tiles form a quadrotor silhouette with four circular rotors, a squashed-X frame, a camera and central fuselage. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Open constellation surround the motif, with staggered terraces along the lower route. 5 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 7 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

Red tiles form a branching tree-of-life motif inspired by Ukrainian embroidery. Blue ground slows the craft; red ground is lethal until captured. Offset garden courts surround the motif, with staggered terraces along the lower route. 4 yellow bouncers, two outer patrols and 8 island-contour patrols guard the field. No horizontal barrier bars. Start at bottom center and reveal 75%.

design.captureConsequence: A new return reshapes the frontier and may move its patrol toward your next departure.

design.counterplay: Use Disruptor Support before committing around a wall tip, then Interceptor Support for the partner’s longer exposed crossing. Approach the platform from opposite ends instead of duplicating one route.
design.lesson: One specialist establishes the winding approach while the other protects the crossing that turns the middle platform into shared ground.
design.mastery: Both craft visit the centre platform after it is connected to the perimeter and each closes a cut, without knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Both craft arrive at one middle platform from opposite ends of the switchback.
design.routeDecision: Bank the outer pockets first, or approach the shared middle platform from opposite wall tips?

design.captureConsequence: The near-aperture closure creates a compact home return; the far-window closure creates an offset departure that shortens a later outside crossing.
design.counterplay: Use the near bands to wait out the patrol, or start the far wrap only when the east keeper and outer patrol are moving away from its return line.
design.lesson: An open square and separated landing change return distance while keeping the known foundation, keeper and perimeter-patrol rules.
design.mastery: Complete both the near-aperture and far-window approaches without a loss.
design.memorableMoment: A Reshetylivka-informed aperture and merezhka rhythm turns the second landing into a short closure or a deliberate long wrap.
design.routeDecision: Close the short near aperture after the perimeter patrol passes, or leave its open side and make the longer outside wrap to the offset far window?

design.captureConsequence: The compass connection lets each pilot stop on permanent ground before choosing the next arrow.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The compass connection lets each pilot stop on permanent ground before choosing the next arrow.
design.routeDecision: Use the upper tailwind to meet at the compass, or develop independent lower returns before exchanging sides?

design.captureConsequence: Anchor order changes which established connections can be relied upon during later captures.
design.counterplay: Use broad cross arms to change departure direction and avoid following the frontier patrol into a narrow return.
design.lesson: Two captured anchors can protect different connections; five foundations are return choices, not five mandatory chores.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors before reaching three quarters of the earned target, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two protected routes support a larger capture without requiring every island to be visited.
design.routeDecision: Bank the western connection first, or secure the eastern anchor while keeping a cross-shaped landing between both eroders?

design.captureConsequence: A spare berth lets a cautious racer recover when the central rover threatens the faster route.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: A spare berth lets a cautious racer recover when the central rover threatens the faster route.
design.routeDecision: Connect the spare berth before expanding east, or cut straight toward the central dock?

design.captureConsequence: The opened bridge remains permanent while nearby reclaimed edges can reopen.
design.counterplay: Choose the next useful return before committing. A new bridge, a neutralized arrow field or a captured hazard can simplify the partner’s next crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The opened bridge remains permanent while nearby reclaimed edges can reopen.
design.routeDecision: Open the permanent relay before confronting erosion, or capture the source and approach the switch from a quiet flank?

design.captureConsequence: Near-row-first creates a compact safe staging lane; refuge-first establishes a deeper return that shortens the second hazardous enclosure.
design.counterplay: The home spine supports several departures. Read the frontier patrol before using the inner gap, or take the longer outer shoulder while both keepers are moving away.
design.lesson: Reshetylivka-whitework-informed open brackets narrow the useful approaches without becoming returns; the two lethal rows still neutralize only through capture.
design.mastery: Connect the east refuge and neutralize both lethal rows without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Alternating open and solid brackets make the two visually balanced hazard rows demand deliberately different routes.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize the near lethal row through the short openwork bracket, or use the long outer shoulder to establish the east refuge before crossing either hazard?

design.captureConsequence: Permanent landings stay intact while a clearly marked reclaimed edge may reopen.
design.counterplay: Build routes between permanent landings. Capturing a Team source stops its future erosion; pilot and recovery anchors are protected.
design.lesson: Erosion reopens reclaimed field; permanent foundations remain safe. Team sources mark one nearby edge tile before removing it.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Permanent landings stay intact while a clearly marked reclaimed edge may reopen.
design.routeDecision: Capture the erosion source early, or build a chain of permanent foundations beyond its local reach?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: Caps follow patrol circuits; hoods seek distant refuges; scarves follow committed switchback routes.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Cross a staggered passage instead of matching every target turn.

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: The guard warns before firing; its body and every humanoid target remain one-contact catches. Hunt points are optional.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Keep a return behind the craft while following the committed branch.
design.routeDecision: Keep a return behind the craft while following the committed branch.

design.captureConsequence: An approach capture creates useful return ground without automatically defeating the core. The same exposed-stage release rule applies.
design.counterplay: The walls block turns and never close cuts. The frontier follows your new return edge; the roamer activates on reclaimed ground.
design.lesson: Deep receiver galleries share the Sentinel field. Choose returns outside the baffles before committing to an inner cut.
design.mastery: Capture the lower receiver before the upper receiver, in separate closures, and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The second receiver approach becomes visible beyond the first gallery wall.
design.routeDecision: Secure the upper gallery approach first, or the lower landing, before turning around a receiver baffle?

design.captureConsequence: A cleared freight lane saves time only if the player also leaves room to avoid the awakened rover.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.

design.memorableMoment: A cleared freight lane saves time only if the player also leaves room to avoid the awakened rover.

design.captureConsequence: Connecting the circuit reshapes both field and reclaimed-ground danger without changing the capture contract.
design.counterplay: Watch the carrier’s trail strike and the current patrol route; close early enough to preserve an exit from a newly awakened roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known impact, frontier and reclaimed-ground rules. This optional Remix adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active impact after the roamer activates and neutralize the lethal bank without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An impact is extinguished at the return just as a new escape corridor becomes necessary.
design.routeDecision: Keep disconnected fallback landings or connect a circuit that gives both the craft and frontier patrol new routes?

design.captureConsequence: The final cut uses a return chosen to survive the territory pressure.
design.counterplay: Connect permanent landings and watch the eroder before relying on a newly captured return.
design.lesson: Moving eroders reopen reclaimed field. Permanent foundations remain safe.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The final cut uses a return chosen to survive the territory pressure.
design.routeDecision: Secure the permanent circuit before racing for coverage, or silence both eroders and finish across reclaimed ground?

design.captureConsequence: Each added connection shortens both partners’ routes, but an enclosure can also introduce pressure on that connection.
design.counterplay: The middle wall has two distinct bypasses. Keep the lethal pocket outside cuts until enclosed and avoid funneling both craft into the same active roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known return networks, material decisions and wake-up timing without learning another rule.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers and connect both intermediate islands to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Four separated islands become a shared network with two moving reclaimed-ground threats.
design.routeDecision: Reach opposite stepping islands first, or connect along one flank and let a partner reopen the other approach?

design.captureConsequence: Removing one bed opens a different flank for the partner while the other bed still demands a detour.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Removing one bed opens a different flank for the partner while the other bed still demands a detour.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize one dangerous bed with an outer loop, or join the high orchard bank first?

design.captureConsequence: Two landings make the final approach independent of any single fragile connector.
design.counterplay: Connect permanent landings and watch the eroder before relying on a newly captured return.
design.lesson: Moving eroders reopen reclaimed field. Permanent foundations remain safe.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: Two landings make the final approach independent of any single fragile connector.
design.routeDecision: Hedge the coast with two safe landings, or pursue a fast broad capture near the eroder?

design.captureConsequence: The fast crossing becomes ordinary reclaimed territory and may be used by the roamer. Outer stepping returns remain useful after the reveal.
design.counterplay: The centre remains efficient during emitter recovery and the upper step remains the quieter first close. The former fixed slow pickup now warns, expires and relocates among three field approaches, so collecting it requires a deliberate exposed detour.
design.lesson: A Krolevets towel record informs triangular side cadence and scattered-centre organization only. The small baffles mark route rhythm without becoming return ground.
design.mastery: Bank the upper step first, connect the centre and lower step, then clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A missed slow window disappears beside one stepping return and later signals from another while the awakened roamer changes which detour is attractive.
design.routeDecision: Take the exposed long centre crossing before the lane warning, or climb the home rail and bank the upper stepping return before waking reclaimed-ground pressure?

design.captureConsequence: Each visible relay persists and the dock connector remains non-scoring. Captures still fill only enemy-free components and can wake the roamer.
design.counterplay: The dock is the fastest permanent return. The south wing takes longer but separates the next departure from the frontier and the awakened roamer.
design.lesson: A museum tile record informs centre-to-four-points organization only. The finale still uses the familiar capture, relay and reclaimed-ground rules.
design.mastery: Establish the south wing first, visit the central dock and both far platforms, then clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Four relay approaches orbit a distinct centre while the player decides which permanent return should become home first.
design.routeDecision: Use the short central dock close and accept immediate frontier pressure, or descend from home to establish the south wing before choosing the four-relay order?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralizing terrain and protecting a return connection solve different parts of the same route.
design.counterplay: Keep the middle reserve and choose an approach outside the active roamer’s reclaimed domain.
design.lesson: Capture order should make the next route easier, not demand that every repeated cluster be cleared.
design.mastery: Neutralize both marked terrain areas and capture both anchors without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An awkward stagger becomes a useful diagonal sequence of axis-aligned captures.
design.routeDecision: Secure the slowing northern connection first, or enclose the southern danger pocket before banking its anchor?

design.captureConsequence: A captured belt loses both its hazard and arrow effect where reclaimed. A line-only connection can still improve the next return without a large reveal.
design.counterplay: The center gaps avoid lethal field. Read both keeper positions before a large enclosure; the separated terraces offer shorter closures and an optional freeze detour.
design.lesson: Combine established terrain neutralization, enemy-retained regions and changing-frontier routes. A marked crossing changes exposure time, not control direction.
design.mastery: Reclaim both lethal side fields completely and visit the connected lower terrace before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: A threatening striped belt becomes an ordinary sideways return while the frontier patrol takes its new contour.
design.routeDecision: Cross the open center between the three belts, or enclose a hazardous side belt to create a wider return?

design.captureConsequence: An early bridge exchanges a smaller first bank for a faster next departure.
design.counterplay: Choose which new return is most useful before choosing which relay to capture first.
design.lesson: Capture each required relay to open its matching permanent bridge. Choose an order that shortens later cuts.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: An early bridge exchanges a smaller first bank for a faster next departure.
design.routeDecision: Open the near bridge before banking coverage, or reach the relay from the longer outer loop?

design.captureConsequence: A reclaimed neck removes its speed penalty and changes the value of the next central crossing.
design.counterplay: Compare the keeper positions with both nearby landings. Cross an arrow band at right angles when its direction is unhelpful.
design.lesson: Shortest distance and shortest exposure need not be the same. Across an arrow is ordinary speed, not a sideways push.
design.mastery: Reclaim both central necks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An initially awkward against-arrow route becomes the best ordinary-speed connection after capture.
design.routeDecision: Use the short central neck against the lower arrows or take the longer lateral approach with them?

design.captureConsequence: A chain built by both pilots turns the final long crossing into several short returns.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A chain built by both pilots turns the final long crossing into several short returns.
design.routeDecision: Create a complete island network before enclosing bays, or alternate bank-and-expand duties from opposite sides?

design.captureConsequence: The same step is a useful short closure before activation and a place to keep moving afterward.
design.counterplay: Leave both ends of the stepped platform usable and depart again when the roamer approaches.
design.lesson: A return closes the trail but does not protect the craft from an active roamer approaching along reclaimed ground.
design.mastery: Use both ends of the stepped foundation for closures after activating the roamer.
design.memorableMoment: A familiar return surface becomes a timing choice without changing the capture rule.
design.routeDecision: Return to the short upper step or the long lower arm while the warned roamer patrols the stepped foundation?

design.captureConsequence: Opposite captures can build a shared central corridor. A line-only closure still supplies a return route while occupied regions stay unclaimed.
design.counterplay: The west spine offers several returns; the east refuge has clear upper and lower bypasses. Watch both keepers before a long vertical cut.
design.lesson: A partner can neutralize material for both craft; the lethal bed must be enclosed before either craft crosses it.
design.mastery: Neutralize both material beds with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: One partner opens the marked crossing while the other turns a slow approach into ordinary shared ground.
design.routeDecision: Split the outer bypasses to enclose both material beds, or first link a shared return through the slow approach?

design.captureConsequence: A chamber clear can move its main danger onto the shared perimeter without completing the other chamber.
design.counterplay: Keep a perimeter connection in each chamber. The divider blocks movement and cannot close a cut; use Support if a roamer approaches a return.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber keeps its own field, while each reclaimed roamer changes the local return route.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent wake-up decisions meet on a common perimeter.
design.routeDecision: Wake the depot roamers together, or let one partner secure a return while the other changes their chamber?

design.captureConsequence: A landing connection improves your next escape without clearing the other occupied bay. Neither bay alone reaches the coverage target.
design.counterplay: The northern landing offers a short return. Watch the bolt before extending your trail; close before its impact reaches you. Use the center deck to change bays, and never mistake a wall for a return.
design.lesson: Only the bolt carrier sends travelling impacts. The two lower keepers break a trail immediately; each occupied bay retains its own field.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active travelling impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small landing return extinguishes an impact; the lower bay then asks for a different enclosure around its baffles.

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. The adapted actor still retains its occupied field region, while the existing wall, foundation and patrol rules remain unchanged.
design.counterplay: Depart behind the outer patrol, use an inner return strip to cancel pursuit, and keep the next alternating passage open.
design.lesson: Alternating rushnyk-inspired openings change which side offers cover; pursuit and the outer patrol pressure different parts of the route.
design.mastery: Cancel pursuit through both inner passages without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A left-to-right escape cancels pursuit, then the mirrored band demands the opposite approach.
design.routeDecision: Cross through the nearer alternating band before pursuit commits, or circle the end while preserving an inner strip as the fallback return?

design.captureConsequence: Closing the centre run neutralizes its directional field. Closing on the west landing instead establishes an offset return while both occupied central regions remain active.
design.counterplay: The centre run is faster but commits directly between both keepers. The west detour delays departure, avoids the shared line and leaves the central landing available for a later ambitious cut.
design.lesson: A museum towel record informs central-diamond, staggered-triangle and outward-branch organization only. Walls block movement; arrows change speed only in unclaimed field and never force a turn.
design.mastery: Use the west landing first, later neutralize the marked centre run and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The visually dominant marked route is not always the safest first closure, and the chosen branch permanently changes the next departure.
design.routeDecision: Use the short marked centre run before the eastern keeper crosses it, or travel west on the perimeter and take the slower chevron-side landing for a quieter first return?

design.captureConsequence: The fast crossing becomes ordinary reclaimed territory and may be used by the roamer. Outer stepping returns remain useful after the reveal.
design.counterplay: The centre is efficient while the emitter recovers. The upper step offers a shorter cut and preserves the middle landing for the roamer’s first pass.
design.lesson: A Krolevets towel record informs triangular side cadence and scattered-centre organization only. The small baffles mark route rhythm without becoming return ground.
design.mastery: Bank the upper step first, connect the centre and lower step, then clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A direct centre shortcut and a stepped side approach exchange value once the roamer activates.
design.routeDecision: Take the exposed long centre crossing before the lane warning, or climb the home rail and bank the upper stepping return before waking reclaimed-ground pressure?

design.captureConsequence: Reconnecting the spine creates a useful route that both active roamers may also use.
design.counterplay: Use broad gaps and distinct upper/lower returns, neutralize marked pockets by enclosure and leave a fresh departure ready.
design.lesson: Combine known retention, return-ground, terrain and threat-domain rules; no new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Join the three spine segments and activate both roamers without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An apparently broken return network becomes useful only after choosing how to keep it escapable.
design.routeDecision: Reconnect the broken spine, or first establish a vertical escape before the two sleepers gain access to it?

design.captureConsequence: Each captured trigger removes a different return detour; opening never performs a second hidden flood.
design.counterplay: Read the inner keeper before a short closure and keep the broad lower opening as an alternative to the gated route.
design.lesson: The field keeper, not a closed gate, retains each chamber. Numbered links change player routes without moving that keeper into another region.
design.mastery: Open the lower connector first and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: The inner link opens while the neighbouring keeper remains in exactly the same field component.
design.routeDecision: Open the cross-ring link before taking the inner trigger, or use the open lower approach and preserve the shorter return for later?

design.captureConsequence: An interior return separates the partner’s lane timing from the outside patrol’s position.
design.counterplay: Choose the next useful return before committing. A new bridge, a neutralized arrow field or a captured hazard can simplify the partner’s next crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: An interior return separates the partner’s lane timing from the outside patrol’s position.
design.routeDecision: Create an interior return before the patrol and lane overlap, or exploit the quiet shore while the warning source rests?

design.captureConsequence: Anchor order determines which connection survives the two eroders. A corner landing changes the next approach without making every island mandatory.
design.counterplay: Use the central cross to change side before the frontier arrives. Enter each wall group through its open face and preserve an uncrowded landing for repair.
design.lesson: A UNESCO Örnek record informs grouped geometry and joined small elements only. Broken bands are walls, while five permanent landings remain route choices rather than five chores.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors from opposite panel openings before reaching three quarters of the earned target, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One banked route remains intact inside a grouped chamber while the opposite unprotected connection visibly reopens.
design.routeDecision: Bank the western anchor through the upper grouped-panel opening, or secure an eastern landing first and approach its lower anchor from the central cross?

design.captureConsequence: The permanent connector preserves the final approach even when surrounding coverage changes.
design.counterplay: Plan the next return before committing. A bridge, cleared arrow band or captured hazard can simplify your final crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The permanent connector preserves the final approach even when surrounding coverage changes.
design.routeDecision: Open a permanent bridge before the eroder reaches the new frontier, or capture the source with a wider first bank?

design.captureConsequence: Both chambers contribute to the same coverage quota. Neither half alone can supply the required clear.
design.counterplay: The divider blocks movement and never banks a trail. Return to an island or the perimeter; each chamber has a visible keeper.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber needs its own useful capture; closing one side does not clear the other.
design.mastery: Each craft closes in its starting chamber and connects its island to the perimeter without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent enclosures transform opposite halves of one board.
design.routeDecision: Work opposite chambers in parallel, or travel around the perimeter to help the pressured partner?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting one branch changes the frontier route and launch angle without granting the opposite quadrant. Corner neutralization remains a deliberate follow-up.
design.counterplay: West-first gives a short hook around the slow approach. East-first crosses during a rest window, then uses the floating end to enclose a lethal corner from outside.
design.lesson: A museum gerdan record informs only paired branching cadence. The two branches stay independent return networks and their wall accents remain blocking geometry.
design.mastery: Connect both branches, neutralize both lethal corners and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The locked column divides the paired branches, forcing a visible choice between a short west hook and the more valuable east approach.
design.routeDecision: Connect the west hooked branch before the column lock reaches it, or establish the longer east branch and attack a dangerous corner from its floating end?

design.captureConsequence: Your chamber order changes which wall tip is exposed on the next return.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.

design.mastery: Complete both chamber orders on equal starting settings.
design.memorableMoment: The last enclosure crosses a lane created by the first.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the north-east opening first, or bank the lower island before approaching the western chamber?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.

design.memorableMoment: Connect a middle return to cover three possible goal routes.

design.captureConsequence: A west-hook closure creates a short staging return; an east-hook closure shifts the useful frontier toward the far side of the slow field.
design.counterplay: The small link return supports a cautious western route; the eastern hook is faster only when both keepers leave its open approach.

design.mastery: Use both hooks and the link return without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A Slobozhanshchyna-rushnyk-informed long field and chain-like linkage create two differently pressured hooks.
design.routeDecision: Build from the west hook along the slow-field edge, or cross the wider ordinary approach and establish the eastern hook first?

design.captureConsequence: A first closure establishes an approach without changing the Sentinel contract. Capturing the shield still opens the explicit core stage; no wall becomes return ground.
design.counterplay: The centre is the shortest return but leaves the frontier beside the next departure. The west landing delays entry, then provides a quieter angle on the chamber opening.
design.lesson: A museum chest record informs tripartite and divided-ridge organization only. Carved-looking baffles are walls; only foundations and reclaimed territory close a cut.
design.mastery: Bank the west upper landing first, disable the chamber shield and release the core without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The broad central route and the side landing lead to the same shield through meaningfully different patrol timing.
design.routeDecision: Close quickly on the central ridge and accept both patrol domains for the shield approach, or travel west on the perimeter and bank the upper side landing before entering the chamber?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Plan crossings and opposite approaches. In Team, both bodies are hazards and every catch advances the shared goal. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try the numbered target order for bonus points. Any contact or enclosure still clears that target; a missed order never blocks completion.
design.memorableMoment: Keep separate exits around the guard corridor; Team Support and rescue remain available.
design.routeDecision: Keep separate exits around the guard corridor; Team Support and rescue remain available. Starts with capacity 14; grows 2 per catch, up to 28. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: The high refuge gives the cutting partner a return that does not depend on Support being ready.
design.counterplay: Keep a second return in reserve; a partner’s new bank can shorten your exposed trail.
design.lesson: An impact follows its original live cut. Close that cut, or use Interceptor Support near the travelling front.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The high refuge gives the cutting partner a return that does not depend on Support being ready.
design.routeDecision: Escort a short central cut with Interceptor Support, or bank the high refuge before the keeper approaches?

design.captureConsequence: Each connection changes the next usable return and the patrol contour.
design.counterplay: Use the clear sides of the rungs and observe the frontier before returning. The slow lower approach is optional, not a forced precision sprint.
design.lesson: A sequence of deliberate returns can reduce impact exposure more than a single ambitious crossing.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations and close a cut with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The ladder acquires a new rung through the player’s own capture.
design.routeDecision: Build short diagonal connections between staggered landings, or expose a longer trail to reclaim a larger side?

design.captureConsequence: A neutralized apron stops consuming the partner’s warning window.
design.counterplay: Wait on permanent ground during a warning, or take a short return. Capturing a Team emitter disables its future warnings.
design.lesson: A numbered pilot and dashed lane mark the locked warning. Close the original cut before the lane fires.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A neutralized apron stops consuming the partner’s warning window.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the slow cooling apron to improve both returns, or connect the centre without crossing it?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a spoke creates a permanent-speed return while the frontier moves around the newly reclaimed edge.
design.counterplay: Turn on the central platform first and watch the frontier before making a second connection. Open corners provide unmarked alternatives.
design.lesson: Changing the frontier changes patrol routes, but never rotates arrows or alters their strength.
design.mastery: Connect three outer windbreaks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Four visibly different approaches converge on one platform without forced spinning or drift.
design.routeDecision: Follow one spoke to a broad windbreak or cross between spokes to shape a shorter frontier?

design.captureConsequence: Connection order changes the fastest return route and which marked channel can be neutralized next.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower clear approaches remain available; the freeze detour is optional.
design.lesson: Combine known terrain and patrol rules; no new mandatory mechanic is introduced.
design.mastery: Link all three refuges without collecting the optional freeze.
design.memorableMoment: Three separated refuges become a route network through two distinct kinds of field.
design.routeDecision: Link the near and central refuges through slow ground, or loop around the marked channel to the far landing?

design.captureConsequence: The growing network changes field and reclaimed-ground threat domains in different ways.
design.counterplay: The permanent hub cannot erode but can still host a roamer; preserve a fresh departure and do not confuse permanence with immunity from enemies.
design.lesson: Combine known erosion, anchor, roamer and frontier rules. No new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors, make a repair and close a cut after the hub roamer activates, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A damaged network still offers a deliberate escape because its essential connections were banked.
design.routeDecision: Bank two useful connections while routing around reclaimed-ground pressure, or take a larger capture while leaving a reserve return?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a spoke creates a permanent-speed return while the frontier moves around the newly reclaimed edge.
design.counterplay: Turn on the central platform first and watch the frontier before making a second connection. Open corners provide unmarked alternatives.
design.lesson: Changing the frontier changes patrol routes, but never rotates arrows or alters their strength.
design.mastery: Connect three outer windbreaks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Four visibly different approaches converge on one platform without forced spinning or drift.
design.routeDecision: Follow one spoke to a broad windbreak or cross between spokes to shape a shorter frontier?

design.captureConsequence: Clearing one chamber contributes shared coverage and frees that pilot to support the other chamber; it never silently clears the occupied field across the divider.
design.counterplay: Use Disruptor Support to create the keeper window in the active chamber and Interceptor Support to protect its longer exposed cut. After banking, travel the perimeter rather than treating the divider as a return.
design.lesson: Each specialist secures a different occupied chamber, then can redeploy around the shared perimeter to protect the partner’s remaining closure.
design.mastery: Each craft closes in its starting chamber and connects its island to the perimeter without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Two independent enclosures transform opposite halves of one board.
design.routeDecision: Work opposite chambers in parallel, or travel around the perimeter to help the pressured partner?

design.captureConsequence: Every new return can shorten a chase or provide cover; capture 50% as well as meeting the quota.
design.counterplay: Keep an island return nearby and distinguish humanoids from the two retaining keepers.
design.lesson: Combine the same contact, enclosure and fixed-aim rules. Any three of the five humanoids satisfy the quota.
design.mastery: Finish with both a contact elimination and an enclosure elimination.
design.memorableMoment: Finish with both a contact elimination and an enclosure elimination.
design.routeDecision: Connect the stepping stones, intercept one runner and enclose another while planning around guard warnings.

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: The guard warns before firing; its body and every humanoid target remain one-contact catches. Hunt points are optional.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Choose cover or a shorter interception across the warning lane.
design.routeDecision: Choose cover or a shorter interception across the warning lane.

design.captureConsequence: Capturing one row opens route choices without requiring the second row to be crossed.
design.counterplay: Use the broad upper and lower bypasses, then return to a foundation or earned ground.
design.lesson: Clear lanes between lethal rows are still unclaimed field, not guaranteed return ground.
design.mastery: Neutralize at least one marked row and connect both refuges without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A long protected spine offers several departures into the same changing hazard problem.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize the nearer row from the spine, or loop around the ends to reach the far refuge first?

design.captureConsequence: The dogleg’s far side becomes a useful launch only after a deliberate bank around its tip.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The dogleg’s far side becomes a useful launch only after a deliberate bank around its tip.
design.routeDecision: Round the dogleg into the southern bay, or take the northern island and return along the outside?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing the source stops future erosion and preserves the partner’s newly built return.
design.counterplay: Build routes between permanent landings. Capturing a Team source stops its future erosion; pilot and recovery anchors are protected.
design.lesson: Erosion reopens reclaimed field; permanent foundations remain safe. Team sources mark one nearby edge tile before removing it.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Capturing the source stops future erosion and preserves the partner’s newly built return.
design.routeDecision: Connect the stable shores first, or let one pilot suppress the source while the other expands?

design.captureConsequence: Connecting a lens pad reshapes the patrol contour on that side without clearing the other keeper’s occupied field.
design.counterplay: Depart away from the frontier patrol. Read the keeper inside the chosen approach and keep the opposite lens pad available before extending around a shoulder.
design.lesson: The opposing work-mat panels block movement but remain open field problems. Lens pads close cuts; keeper positions decide what fills.
design.mastery: Make a closure from each lens pad, using a facing opening and an exterior shoulder without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The eastern landing needs a dogleg around a detached shoulder after the direct western connection.
design.routeDecision: Take the direct western lens approach, or bend above or below the eastern panel shoulder before returning to its landing?

design.captureConsequence: The opened bridge protects a useful finish even while neighboring reclaimed field erodes.
design.counterplay: Connect permanent landings and watch the eroder before relying on a newly captured return.
design.lesson: Moving eroders reopen reclaimed field. Permanent foundations remain safe.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The opened bridge protects a useful finish even while neighboring reclaimed field erodes.
design.routeDecision: Open the permanent shortcut, or enclose the eroder before seeking the relay?

design.captureConsequence: The southern pier becomes a shared launch into both bays; a northern bridge leaves a larger final enclosure.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The southern pier becomes a shared launch into both bays; a northern bridge leaves a larger final enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Meet at the southern pier, or secure a northern bridge around the wall tip?

design.captureConsequence: A closure changes the contour that the patrol follows; it does not become a field-retaining enemy.
design.counterplay: The first return approaches the broad top of the island, away from the patrol on its left edge.
design.lesson: Unlike the outer patrol, a frontier patrol follows the changing field/reclaimed boundary.
design.mastery: Create a new frontier and depart from a different edge.
design.memorableMoment: The newly reclaimed edge becomes part of the patrol route.
design.routeDecision: Close ahead of the moving frontier patrol, or shape a return on the opposite side of its route?

design.captureConsequence: A capture changes your return options but can create an eligible frontier for erosion.
design.counterplay: Watch the eroder stop and mark a cell. Keep a permanent return within reach instead of chasing every lost cell.
design.lesson: The marked cell warns before reopening. Foundations remain permanent; earned ground can need repair.
design.mastery: Repair an eroded cell with a legal closure without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small gap reopens beside a landing that stays intact.
design.routeDecision: Use the permanent landing for repeated returns, or bank a larger exposed edge that the eroder can reopen?

design.captureConsequence: Central-first play creates several short departures under roamer pressure; east-first play preserves an independent landing before the hub is connected.
design.counterplay: The central stem is short but becomes contested after activation. The east window costs a longer exposed route and leaves a separate escape beyond the roamer network.
design.lesson: Reshetylivka-cutwork-inspired openings are formed from walls and empty field. Only reclaimed foundations close a cut, and waking a roamer changes the value of the central return.
design.mastery: Activate the central roamer, then close at both an outer window and the central stem without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A light-and-dark cutwork rhythm turns the shortest connection into the return that becomes dangerous first.
design.routeDecision: Close the short central cutwork window and wake its roamer, or pass the offset square openings to establish the east window first?

design.captureConsequence: A broad neutralized band becomes the team’s crossing lane between two narrow approaches.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A broad neutralized band becomes the team’s crossing lane between two narrow approaches.
design.routeDecision: Weave through the narrow unpainted corridors, or enclose a broad slow band to simplify the partner’s route?

design.captureConsequence: Reading the keeper rather than the rival decides which return can close before impact.
design.counterplay: Keep two possible returns and watch the keeper before choosing the longer enclosure.
design.lesson: Travelling impacts follow a live cut. Close onto a prepared return before the impact catches you.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: Reading the keeper rather than the rival decides which return can close before impact.
design.routeDecision: Race through the central opening, or wait for the keeper to leave the shorter western line?

design.captureConsequence: The outer bank makes a wider final enclosure possible without treating a wall as safe ground.

design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The outer bank makes a wider final enclosure possible without treating a wall as safe ground.
design.routeDecision: Leave the open court by the inside lane, or bank its outer edge before crossing?

design.captureConsequence: A direct relay cut changes the shelf from an obstacle into the safest final landing.
design.counterplay: Choose which new return is most useful before choosing which relay to capture first.
design.lesson: Capture each required relay to open its matching permanent bridge. Choose an order that shortens later cuts.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: A direct relay cut changes the shelf from an obstacle into the safest final landing.
design.routeDecision: Approach the shelf relay directly, or surround the lower bay before turning toward it?

design.captureConsequence: Both partners finish with access to a circuit whose individual links they secured for each other.

design.lesson: An impact follows its original live cut. Close that cut, or use Interceptor Support near the travelling front.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Both partners finish with access to a circuit whose individual links they secured for each other.
design.routeDecision: Build a shared observatory circuit in stages, or alternate short safe banks with one long protected cut?

design.captureConsequence: Capture order determines which branch remains a convenient return under pressure.

design.memorableMoment: The best next capture opens a way out rather than maximizing immediate area.
design.routeDecision: Build an outside escape to the near platform, or neutralize the marked pocket before joining the far platform?

design.captureConsequence: An inner landing shortens a later cut without banking against a wall. Outer returns introduce reclaimed-ground pressure, and two retainers keep each chamber contested until deliberately enclosed.
design.counterplay: The top and bottom baffle ends stay open. Watch both local keepers before crossing; after waking a roamer, turn onto a different return rather than waiting on its new rail. Either partner may travel around the divider to help. Coordinate the Interceptor around exposed lines and the Disruptor around moving threats; neither pulse substitutes for the other.
design.lesson: Interceptor Support removes nearby travelling impacts while Disruptor Support slows nearby enemies. Rescue remains available to both players.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.

design.routeDecision: Wake the outer return patrols for quick perimeter access, or wrap the inner baffles to establish receiver landings first?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Combine long tails, deliberate returns, guards and optional ordered catches. Clear every target by either legal method. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try the numbered target order for bonus points. Any contact or enclosure still clears that target; a missed order never blocks completion.
design.memorableMoment: Weave between the staggered screens with a long body; optional order never prevents a clear.
design.routeDecision: Weave between the staggered screens with a long body; optional order never prevents a clear. Starts with capacity 18; grows 3 per catch, up to 39. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.

design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Turn the refuge seeker away from a long exposed chase.

design.captureConsequence: An outer enclosure can remove a garden and an approach together, giving the other craft a full-speed return.
design.counterplay: Keep the lethal gardens outside your route until they are reclaimed. Time the central keeper before attempting a shared bridge.
design.lesson: A short route through slow field can keep a trail exposed longer than an outer bypass.
design.mastery: Neutralize every slow and lethal patch with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two dangerous gardens become ordinary shared ground around a contested middle island.
design.routeDecision: Link through a slow approach to reach the middle island, or split the outer routes and clear the gardens first?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Compare persistent tails with missions that shed segments on a field-to-safe return. Choose when to bank your route. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.

design.memorableMoment: One shared bridge supports two different chamber problems.

design.captureConsequence: Every bridge creates a new possible closure; no route requires a lucky bonus.

design.lesson: Choose a route using both return distance and the future shape of retained regions.
design.mastery: Join the two side outposts without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The final bridge turns separated outposts into a useful loop.

design.captureConsequence: The upper join leaves a broad lower region; the lower gathered join leaves a different upper region and a closer angle to the east shoulder.
design.counterplay: Use the west shoulder as safe staging, then commit above or below only when the corresponding keeper is travelling away from the intended line.

design.routeDecision: Join through the upper shoulder group for the shorter first return, or descend to the offset gathered group for a longer line that approaches the far shoulder?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.

design.captureConsequence: Relay corners stay permanent while erosion can restore a marked inner spoke. Carrier impacts still disappear when a valid closure secures the trail.

design.captureConsequence: New links change route length; the keepers still determine which regions fill.

design.captureConsequence: The first reclaimed bed determines which side offers a shorter, faster next route.

design.routeDecision: Ride the central down-arrow to the joined landing before a keeper contests it, or reposition west and close on the upper riser while preserving the centre for an emitter recovery window?

design.captureConsequence: The selected first relay decides which pilot gets the next short crossing.
