design.memorableMoment: One straight assisted closure turns the alternating side openings into the more valuable second problem instead of repeating another spoke.
design.routeDecision: Take the short marked north thread, or cross west through the alternating band openings to reshape the frontier before approaching another return?

design.captureConsequence: A completed approach allows the next pilot to attack the new target with less trail exposed.
design.counterplay: Prepare the next return while completing the current objective. Dashed crossed targets are still protected; a warning never requires a synchronized button press.
design.lesson: Team targets open in numbered order and require separate captures. Prepare a return for the next active target.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A completed approach allows the next pilot to attack the new target with less trail exposed.
design.routeDecision: Let the Interceptor cover the active target, or use separate short cuts to create a safe approach before each stage?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. Field-retaining enemies still determine which regions remain unclaimed, and the existing terrain or patrol consequences remain active.
design.counterplay: Keep the northern landing in reserve. Close before the committed approach arrives, or put reclaimed ground or a wall between the pursuer and the next exposed trail.
design.lesson: The pursuer warns, locks one observed point on the unfinished trail, and commits for a finite route. It never retargets invisibly during that commitment.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active travelling impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A short landing closure cancels a visibly committed pursuit before the lower bay asks for a different route.
design.routeDecision: Close at the nearby northern landing when pursuit locks, or risk the longer lower enclosure while the committed route remains visible?

design.captureConsequence: Material neutralization and roamer activation can occur in the same enclosure; both partners must read the changed board.
design.counterplay: Use the side spines to change departure heights. Enclose crosses before entering them and leave space around the courtyard when a roamer wakes.
design.lesson: Removing a terrain hazard does not make every reclaimed route free of enemies.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers and connect the courtyard to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: A dangerous garden becomes passable just as the tracked bodies make the surrounding ground busy.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize the upper hazard before linking the courtyard, or establish the lower slow-field approach while the partner prepares a different exit?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing one bay does not remove the keeper from the other.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: A starting return lane can separate two independently retained regions.
design.mastery: Earn territory on both sides without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same central lane supports two different enclosure rhythms.
design.routeDecision: Work one bay to completion or alternate sides to follow the safer keeper positions?

design.captureConsequence: The required capture banks a stable return connection instead of merely adding a completion checkbox.
design.counterplay: Connect the anchor to useful reclaimed ground before the next enclosure; other earned cells remain vulnerable.
design.lesson: A captured required objective protects its cell and one deterministic reclaimed path to a permanent foundation or outer rail.
design.mastery: Capture the anchor before reaching half of the earned coverage target, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One protected connection survives while neighboring earned frontier remains erodible.
design.routeDecision: Capture the crossing anchor before expanding farther, or use the lower permanent lane to approach from the opposite side?

design.captureConsequence: North-first neutralizes the slow approach and banks one protected objective. South-east-first removes immediate danger and creates a stronger but erodible repair corridor.
design.counterplay: Keep the central foundation in reserve. West-first shortens the anchor capture; east-first avoids the reclaimed roamer but leaves a longer repair route behind the lethal field.
design.lesson: Borshchiv embroidery informs alternating visual density only. Staggered walls shape repairs while foundations remain permanent and earned territory remains erodible.
design.mastery: Capture both anchors, neutralize both terrain fields and repair one reopened link.
design.memorableMoment: Alternating dense and open shoulders make the same diagonal island sequence support a cautious anchor route or an exposed repair race.
design.routeDecision: Bank the slowed northern anchor through the narrow western shoulder, or cross the open east repair gap to enclose the lethal pocket before an eroder reopens the earned route?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Plan crossings and opposite approaches. In Team, both bodies are hazards and every catch advances the shared goal. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Choose who uses the inner detour first; the outer shore remains available to the other route.
design.routeDecision: Choose who uses the inner detour first; the outer shore remains available to the other route. Starts with capacity 13; grows 2 per catch, up to 27. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: A new return reshapes the frontier and may move its patrol toward your next departure.
design.counterplay: Depart from the side away from the frontier patrol and choose a return before entering an opening.
design.lesson: This egg-decoration-inspired outline stays open; walls cannot create a secretly empty sealed chamber.
design.mastery: Use one side opening and one stepped end opening.
design.memorableMoment: An inward enclosure changes which opening is useful on the next outward cut.
design.routeDecision: Leave the central spindle through a side opening, or reach past the segmented oval end?

design.captureConsequence: The saved lens gives a threatened partner a new landing after the outer routes have become long.
design.counterplay: Keep a second return in reserve; a partner’s new bank can shorten your exposed trail.
design.lesson: An impact follows its original live cut. Close that cut, or use Interceptor Support near the travelling front.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The saved lens gives a threatened partner a new landing after the outer routes have become long.
design.routeDecision: Save the centre lens as a late refuge, or connect it immediately and divide the outer bays?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Read elbows, pockets and switchbacks before the body reaches them. The shortest line is not always the easiest turn. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Use the broad pockets between posts to turn before chasing a runner into the next lane.
design.routeDecision: Use the broad pockets between posts to turn before chasing a runner into the next lane. Starts with capacity 7; grows 1 per catch, up to 11. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: Reconnecting the spine creates a useful route that both active roamers may also use.
design.counterplay: Use broad gaps and distinct upper/lower returns, neutralize marked pockets by enclosure and leave a fresh departure ready.
design.lesson: Combine known retention, return-ground, terrain and threat-domain rules; no new mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Join the three spine segments and activate both roamers without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An apparently broken return network becomes useful only after choosing how to keep it escapable.
design.routeDecision: Reconnect the broken spine, or first establish a vertical escape before the two sleepers gain access to it?

design.captureConsequence: The repair and enclosure routes trade a small immediate gain for a different final threat.
design.counterplay: Connect permanent landings and watch the eroder before relying on a newly captured return.
design.lesson: Moving eroders reopen reclaimed field. Permanent foundations remain safe.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The repair and enclosure routes trade a small immediate gain for a different final threat.
design.routeDecision: Repair a reopened shortcut, or draw a new outer contour that traps the eroder away from the finish?

design.captureConsequence: The cleared headwind is a shared route whose usefulness survives the next capture.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The cleared headwind is a shared route whose usefulness survives the next capture.
design.routeDecision: Clear the headwind under the windbreak, or cross above it and leave that work for the partner’s shorter approach?

design.captureConsequence: The final active target can be taken from either partner’s prepared approach.
design.counterplay: Prepare the next return while completing the current objective. Dashed crossed targets are still protected; a warning never requires a synchronized button press.
design.lesson: Team targets open in numbered order and require separate captures. Prepare a return for the next active target.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The final active target can be taken from either partner’s prepared approach.
design.routeDecision: Prepare both final approaches while clearing the outer watch stations, or silence a source before committing to the centre?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. The adapted actor still retains its occupied field region, while the existing wall, foundation and patrol rules remain unchanged.
design.counterplay: Choose two reachable pads, wait for the aim point, then turn around the central component wall toward the pad the interceptor did not target.
design.lesson: Interception predicts only the observed heading. The four motor-like pads provide deliberate alternatives after the visible lock.
design.mastery: Feint after a lock and connect all four pads without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A propeller-like four-pad layout turns one warned attack into a satisfying mid-route feint.
design.routeDecision: Keep the direct motor-pad heading after the target locks, or turn toward an adjacent pad and leave the committed intercept behind?

design.captureConsequence: A successful enclosure turns the dangerous center into a new traversable return surface.
design.counterplay: The first return and broad outside approaches avoid the marked bed entirely.
design.lesson: Framed crosses harm the craft on unclaimed field. Capturing that field neutralizes the hazard.
design.mastery: Neutralize the whole central bed without visiting the far landing first.
design.memorableMoment: The crossed warning disappears from earned ground without changing the underlying map rule.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the marked central bed before crossing, or keep a longer clear path around it?

design.captureConsequence: Only the active numbered target can advance the encounter; preparing the next approach gives the partner useful work.
design.counterplay: Prepare the next return while completing the current objective. Dashed crossed targets are still protected; a warning never requires a synchronized button press.
design.lesson: Team targets open in numbered order and require separate captures. Prepare a return for the next active target.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Only the active numbered target can advance the encounter; preparing the next approach gives the partner useful work.
design.routeDecision: Prepare a return near target two while the partner captures target one, or work together on the safer first enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: Each shore connection changes which branch end is a useful next departure; a connection between occupied regions may earn only its trail.
design.counterplay: Keep a second landing within reach and read the keeper beyond the next branch. The broad outer route is an alternative when the central passage is contested.
design.lesson: The bank ornaments are walls, not shore returns. Separate reclaimed platforms close cuts; the field keepers retain their ordinary field regions.
design.mastery: Connect both shores using a central passage and an outer-bank approach before clearing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small central connection opens a new crossing angle, while the far bank still needs a differently shaped enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Link the central landing through the gap between branching banks, or take a wider shore-to-shore crossing around a flower-and-bird silhouette?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing removes live impacts and neutralizes terrain, but may activate a new ground threat without disabling either emitter.
design.counterplay: Shorten the live trail before the marked cross fires and leave an exit on reclaimed ground before capturing the roamer.
design.lesson: Combine known lane, impact and reclaimed-ground threats. A travelling spark has grace; an active lane striking the trail does not.
design.mastery: Clear without a life loss after closing an active-impact cut while the roamer was already active.
design.memorableMoment: A timely closure extinguishes a moving impact while the new ground still offers an escape from the roamer.
design.routeDecision: Spend the rest window linking another refuge, or close a smaller cut and preserve a corridor before the roamer wakes?

design.captureConsequence: The final exchange uses two different material lanes that the partners have each neutralized.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The final exchange uses two different material lanes that the partners have each neutralized.
design.routeDecision: Make the middle garden safe for both pilots, or clear separate outer beds before exchanging sides?

design.captureConsequence: The last bank uses the bridge selected at the beginning of the race.
design.counterplay: Choose which new return is most useful before choosing which relay to capture first.
design.lesson: Capture each required relay to open its matching permanent bridge. Choose an order that shortens later cuts.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The last bank uses the bridge selected at the beginning of the race.
design.routeDecision: Open the central links for a quick final cut, or keep the outer return and claim the broad southern pocket?

design.captureConsequence: The shelter bridge gives either pilot a safe rescue approach during later lane warnings.
design.counterplay: Choose the next useful return before committing. A new bridge, a neutralized arrow field or a captured hazard can simplify the partner’s next crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The shelter bridge gives either pilot a safe rescue approach during later lane warnings.
design.routeDecision: Open the shelter bridge first, or silence the warning source before reaching the numbered relay?

design.captureConsequence: The first shore becomes a safe hinge for a faster second enclosure.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The first shore becomes a safe hinge for a faster second enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Take the nearby shore for an early bank, or pass it to cut off the larger eastern field?

design.captureConsequence: A line-only link can still shorten both routes while occupied regions remain unclaimed.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower keepers leave different departure windows. Use the intermediate islands to shorten exposure; a wall is never a return.
design.lesson: A hit on either unfinished Team line sends visible fronts along that player’s current cut. Bank it before the craft-bound front arrives.
design.mastery: Connect both intermediate islands to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: An offset chain of four islands becomes one shared route network.
design.routeDecision: Take separate stepping stones, or connect across the centre before spreading out?

design.captureConsequence: A landing connection improves your next escape without clearing the other occupied bay. Neither bay alone reaches the coverage target.
design.counterplay: The northern landing offers a short return. Watch every field enemy before extending your trail; close before its impact reaches you. Use the center deck to change bays, and never mistake a wall for a return.
design.lesson: Every field enemy sends a travelling impact when it strikes an unfinished trail; each occupied bay retains its own field.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active travelling impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small landing return extinguishes an impact; the lower bay then asks for a different enclosure around its baffles.
design.routeDecision: Practice a short northern landing return, or work around the lower baffles for a larger enclosure between two keepers?

design.captureConsequence: A useful connection can shorten the next cut without making every cell in that connection permanent.
design.counterplay: Keep the central island as a reserve; neutralize the slow approach by enclosure before relying on it.
design.lesson: Isolated foundations provide dependable landings even when the earned links between them are vulnerable.
design.mastery: Join all three foundations and repair eroded ground without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One return link breaks while the island itself remains available.
design.routeDecision: Join the near island through the slowing approach, or open the wider clear side and retain a second return?

design.captureConsequence: Removing a guard also removes its remaining shots. Reach 35% capture and two eliminations to finish.
design.counterplay: Move away from the warning line or reach reclaimed ground. Ordinary keepers remain dangerous inside and outside the courtyard.
design.lesson: A guard aims at a fixed point before firing. Its body is removable by one touch; its shot can hurt an exposed craft.
design.mastery: Evade a warning and remove its guard without losing a life. Both pilots contribute a capture or hunt elimination.
design.memorableMoment: Evade a warning and remove its guard without losing a life.
design.routeDecision: Let one pilot draw the fixed warning while the partner approaches. Support can intercept a nearby shot; a safe partner can still rescue.

design.captureConsequence: The first receiver advances the visible shield count while the original attack cadence continues. Only the final shield cancels that lane and starts the transition.
design.counterplay: The broken central return leaves the whole field connected initially. Both receivers lie inside the retained chamber; outer captures do not collect them. Keep the northward opening available and stay clear of the core body.
design.lesson: Every listed shield must be captured; one relay does not expose the core. Their display order does not force a route order.
design.mastery: Capture the eastern shield before the western shield, in separate closures, and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Two opposing receiver sites share one Sentinel without a free half-board reveal.
design.routeDecision: Approach the western receiver around the core, or the eastern receiver first, while preserving the five-cell return opening?

design.captureConsequence: Inner-first play reshapes the tight western contour; outer-first play creates a deeper eastern return for the following enclosure.
design.counterplay: The inner fold is quick but close to the western keeper. The outer band is longer and becomes useful when the eastern keeper turns away from its shoulder.
design.lesson: A stepped return can offer several landing lengths while the same moving-frontier rules remain predictable.
design.mastery: Use both the inner fold and outer band as closure surfaces without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A Krolevets-weaving-informed alternation of broad and narrow bands turns one L into two visibly different return rhythms.
design.routeDecision: Close beside the short inner fold, or follow the alternating bands to establish the longer outer shoulder before the frontier arrives?

design.captureConsequence: The south bridge becomes permanent reclaimed ground without awarding coverage or releasing either field keeper.
design.counterplay: Close on the existing platform first. The opened bridge then reaches a second landing without another exposed crossing.
design.lesson: Capture the numbered trigger to open its matching connector. A closed crossbar blocks a cut; an opened connector closes it.
design.mastery: Use the opened bridge to reach the lower landing and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: One short closure visibly joins two separated landings before the next route begins.
design.routeDecision: Land through the visible relay to establish a permanent southward shortcut, or keep using the longer outside return?

design.captureConsequence: The marked shortcut becomes ordinary-speed reclaimed ground. The roamer may now use it too, so the outer stepping platforms retain their value.
design.counterplay: The first broad arrow has a clear landing and no forced turn. Leave the locked column before it fires; retain a second departure when reclaiming the roamer.
design.lesson: A direct arrow route can be efficient without being the best return after a capture. The locked lane and awakened ground domain remain separately readable.
design.mastery: Connect and visit the upper and lower stepping platforms before clearing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The fastest outward route turns into contested reclaimed ground, making the quieter stepping return useful.
design.routeDecision: Use the fast long crossing toward the middle landing, or claim the upper stepping platform before awakening the ground roamer?

design.captureConsequence: The slow-bed closure makes a broad western return; the upper closure creates a narrow eastern departure without neutralizing the hot bed.
design.counterplay: The western line is direct but slow. The upper branch avoids the lethal bed, costs more distance, and exposes a different frontier timing.
design.lesson: The non-crossing branches supply safe staging while the existing slow and lethal beds retain their exact rules and cells.
design.mastery: Close from both branch approaches without entering the lethal bed or losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A flowing, non-crossing branch route lets the player choose a slow garden bed or an ambitious arc above heat.
design.routeDecision: Cross the western slow bed directly from the side branch, or climb the safe stem and arc above the eastern hot bed for a faster but longer enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: A connection around a branch creates a shorter departure, not a free district clear. Neutralizing the eastern hazard creates usable ground until erosion restores its underlying danger; foundations stay protected.
design.counterplay: Inspect the short wall beside the center start, then choose an opening above or below it. Compare the two western branch ends with the eastern middle gap; use the spine when an earned approach erodes.
design.lesson: The alternating kilim-inspired branches are walls, not returns. Both districts retain an eroder and a keeper; the permanent center spine still lets you change districts without losing that refuge.
design.mastery: Close a cut in each district, use a branch end and the eastern middle gap, and neutralize the eastern hazard without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The open flower on one side offers a middle mouth while the longer branch on the other demands a choice of ends.
design.routeDecision: Work around the western branch ends to bank the small island, or pass the eastern flower gap toward its taller return and lethal pocket?

design.captureConsequence: A warning is tied to one pilot’s original cut; closing that cut gives the partner a clear launch.
design.counterplay: Wait on permanent ground during a warning, or take a short return. Capturing a Team emitter disables its future warnings.
design.lesson: A numbered pilot and dashed lane mark the locked warning. Close the original cut before the lane fires.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A warning is tied to one pilot’s original cut; closing that cut gives the partner a clear launch.
design.routeDecision: Close a short connector during the first marked lane, or wait on a landing for the rest window?

design.captureConsequence: Each short connection changes your launch angle without automatically claiming a corner. A later enclosure can neutralize terrain and turn the floating end into a longer return route.
design.counterplay: Shift within the central landing before departing toward either rail. Read the locked column, use the hooked tip as a nearer western return, and enclose lethal corners from outside.
design.lesson: The west hook is return ground that redirects the keeper; the east rail floats short of the border. Connecting a rail is a foothold, not a free quadrant.
design.mastery: Neutralize both lethal corners and connect all three foundations without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: The first rail connection leaves the picture contested; steering around its end turns the next return into a meaningful enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Link the hooked west rail or floating east rail first, then choose a return around its end to enclose a dangerous corner?

design.captureConsequence: An earned connection can extend both the craft’s return network and the awakened rover’s movement domain; the branch walls stay impassable.
design.counterplay: Choose a departure and a second work mat before enclosing the sleeper. Use the unequal branch ends to keep a parallel escape rather than trapping yourself in one earned aisle.
design.lesson: Branching work-mat obstacles are walls, not reclaimed trunks. Capturing the sleeping rover’s field activates pressure on reclaimed ground after its warning.
design.mastery: Wake the rover and then use three different work mats, including an outer escape, without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The central shortcut becomes contested, making the previously established outer mat immediately useful.
design.routeDecision: Reclaim the aisle between staggered branches and wake the rover, or connect an outer work mat first so a parallel escape survives activation?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Use forks and parallel lanes to intercept fleeing humanoids. Optional catch chains reward a planned circuit. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try the numbered target order for bonus points. Any contact or enclosure still clears that target; a missed order never blocks completion.
design.memorableMoment: Combine parallel lanes and open junctions, keeping the tail out of the next interception.
design.routeDecision: Combine parallel lanes and open junctions, keeping the tail out of the next interception. Starts with capacity 11; grows 2 per catch, up to 23. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: The west connector opens approaches on both sides of the baffles, while occupied field still remains unclaimed. Each new frontier changes the patrol route.
design.counterplay: Keep a real landing at the end of the cut. Cross the open aisle during a rest window, or turn around a baffle end after reading the marked column.
design.lesson: A locked column threatens the exposed trail. A west landing and a northern landing offer different returns; baffles are walls, never return surfaces.
design.mastery: Connect all three foundations and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A completed westward connector remains usable through the column attack, then offers a different approach around the upper baffle.
design.routeDecision: Connect the west landing through the open aisle, or establish the northern return before working around the baffle ends?

design.captureConsequence: The short refuge converts a single risky crossing into two smaller exposures.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.

design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The short refuge converts a single risky crossing into two smaller exposures.
design.routeDecision: Commit to the long wave during the keeper’s retreat, or secure a short refuge before entering it?

design.routeDecision: Choose opposite circuits through the landings. Remove the shared six-target population and keep a return available for your partner.

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: Caps follow patrol circuits; hoods seek distant refuges; scarves follow committed switchback routes.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Approach the refuge target from its distant goal.
design.routeDecision: Approach the refuge target from its distant goal.

design.captureConsequence: The cleared garden gives the final cut an easier return even if it starts behind.

design.memorableMoment: The cleared garden gives the final cut an easier return even if it starts behind.

design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The diagonal link pays back its longer first cut on the last approach.
design.routeDecision: Take two short banks, or invest in the diagonal link that removes a later crossing?

design.captureConsequence: The central closure preserves two broad fields; an outer-branch closure creates a farther return that shortens the next exposed crossing.

design.mastery: Complete both the central-stem and outer-branch approaches without a loss.

design.routeDecision: Use the central stem for a short ordinary closure, or commit to a separated outer branch that improves the later return toward an optional bonus window?

design.routeDecision: Thread an opening in a stepped diamond, or take the longer outer route to the next landing?

design.captureConsequence: The finishing choice depends on both the remaining field and the next safe landing.
design.counterplay: Watch the next corner and return behind the patrol, or connect an interior refuge before committing to the shore.
design.lesson: Perimeter patrols follow the outside rail. Permanent interior landings give you an alternative return.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The finishing choice depends on both the remaining field and the next safe landing.
design.routeDecision: Finish through the interior watch line, or exploit the patrol gap for one larger perimeter bank?

design.captureConsequence: The completed route no longer depends on arrow direction, so either partner can finish from either side.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The completed route no longer depends on arrow direction, so either partner can finish from either side.
design.routeDecision: Unify the highland landings through three arrow fields, or secure two ordinary-speed returns before the final crossing?

design.captureConsequence: The near relay opens a permanent non-scoring home dock. Other captures neutralize field only where no keeper remains, and can wake the roamer on reclaimed ground. Captured objectives persist through ordinary recovery.
design.counterplay: Watch both keeper positions before departing; an enemy on each side can leave a line-only capture. Keep an upper or dock return ready before enclosing the ground roamer. The freeze pickup is optional.
design.lesson: The finale combines the familiar enemy-retained capture rule with relay returns and reclaimed-ground pressure. There is no boss shield or release window: enclose the four visible signal objectives and reach the coverage target.
design.mastery: Connect and visit a western wing and either far-eastern platform before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: An opened dock can offer a homeward return after a wide reveal wakes the roamer; choose a return rather than wait for a boss opening.
design.routeDecision: Capture the near relay to open the home dock, or establish a far-wing return while the two field keepers occupy different approaches?

design.captureConsequence: The outer loop costs more exposure but gives both pilots a wide full-speed return.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The outer loop costs more exposure but gives both pilots a wide full-speed return.
design.routeDecision: Clear a narrow crossing over the slow channel, or make an outer loop that removes a whole channel section?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing one bay does not remove the keeper from the other.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: A starting return lane can separate two independently retained regions.
design.mastery: Earn territory on both sides without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same central lane supports two different enclosure rhythms.
design.routeDecision: Work one bay to completion or alternate sides to follow the safer keeper positions?

design.captureConsequence: A pad connection creates a return beyond a frame arm; retaining enemies still determine which side fills.
design.counterplay: Use an adjacent pad for a short closure, observe the keepers across all three aisles, and depart behind the outer patrol.
design.lesson: The four reclaimed pads are real return surfaces; the central component is an impassable wall.
design.mastery: Connect all four pads without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The open frame arms turn four pads into a choice of changing approach directions.
design.routeDecision: Connect an offset motor pad through the inner aisle, or circle a frame arm for a wider enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: The middle lane becomes a late shortcut only for a player who first encloses it.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The middle lane becomes a late shortcut only for a player who first encloses it.
design.routeDecision: Clear a safe outer circuit, or neutralize the middle material lane before the finish?

design.captureConsequence: A reclaimed band gives the partner a predictable return before the next locked warning.
design.counterplay: Choose the next useful return before committing. A new bridge, a neutralized arrow field or a captured hazard can simplify the partner’s next crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A reclaimed band gives the partner a predictable return before the next locked warning.
design.routeDecision: Take the marked fast lane during rest, or neutralize it first so the partner can return against its direction?

design.captureConsequence: The upper shoulder shortens a western enclosure; the lower shoulder creates a safer later departure toward the eastern field.
design.counterplay: Stage on the spine until the nearest keeper travels away, then choose the shoulder that avoids crossing the broader occupied slow bed.
design.lesson: An asymmetric spine changes which slow-field edge is the practical return without changing terrain physics.
design.mastery: Close once from each shoulder without collecting the optional life.
design.memorableMoment: A Bukovyna-pysanka-informed divided spine creates two unequal shoulders between preserved slow fields.
design.routeDecision: Use the upper shoulder to work around the western slow bed, or descend the spine and establish the lower shoulder beside the eastern bed first?

design.captureConsequence: The selected branch becomes permanent return ground. The other compound remains independently enemy-retained, and an awakened roamer may use every opened connector.
design.counterplay: Upper-first creates the safest repeated departure. East-first spends more exposure to neutralize a hazardous court and secure a return before the roamer activates on reclaimed ground.
design.lesson: A museum kilim record informs alternating branch direction and right-angle border rhythm only. Relay order changes the return network while every field keeper stays in its own domain.
design.mastery: Open the east branch first, preserve an escape corridor and clear after visiting all three compounds without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A newly opened branch is simultaneously a valuable shortcut and a future roamer route.
design.routeDecision: Open the short upper relay to gain a direct north return, or branch east through the longer exposed approach and secure the roamer-side connector first?

design.captureConsequence: Filling beside one arm removes old edges and changes the patrol route around the other.
design.counterplay: Watch the marked patrol, return to the broad elbow, and keep the outside approach available.
design.lesson: A frontier patrol follows the changed field edge; its speed does not increase when the route gets shorter.
design.mastery: Connect both ends of the elbow to the outer perimeter without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same L-shaped return becomes a different departure after its inside corner is captured.
design.routeDecision: Close a short cut at the elbow, or use the long arm to redirect the frontier before the next departure?

design.captureConsequence: The final approach has both a permanent refuge and a repaired route into the remaining field.
design.counterplay: Choose the next useful return before committing. A new bridge, a neutralized arrow field or a captured hazard can simplify the partner’s next crossing.

design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The final approach has both a permanent refuge and a repaired route into the remaining field.
design.routeDecision: Build the interior foundations before the patrol arrives, or capture the erosion source to preserve the partner’s outside return?

design.captureConsequence: The last shield location decides the first useful exposed-core approach.
design.counterplay: Prepare the core approach before the last shield. If the open window closes, wait for the next readable attack cycle.
design.lesson: Capture both shield relays in either order, then release the exposed sentinel core with a fresh cut during its open phase.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The last shield location decides the first useful exposed-core approach.
design.routeDecision: Leave the distant shield for last to approach the core from that side, or open it first and return along the lower landings?

design.captureConsequence: A middle rung lets the partner cross between the upper and lower halves without repeating a long exposure.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A middle rung lets the partner cross between the upper and lower halves without repeating a long exposure.
design.routeDecision: Join the middle rungs first, or attach opposite ends of the ladder to the perimeter?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Compare persistent tails with missions that shed segments on a field-to-safe return. Choose when to bank your route. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Catch a target, then return from the field to safe ground to shed two segments.
design.routeDecision: Catch a target, then return from the field to safe ground to shed two segments. Starts with capacity 11; grows 3 per catch, up to 29. A field-to-safe return sheds up to 2 segments.

design.captureConsequence: The captured part loses its arrows and becomes ordinary reclaimed movement, so the return trip uses a different route budget.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before accelerating. The wide marked approach has no required turn at its end; the next direction stays your choice.
design.lesson: Arrows change craft speed only while moving on unclaimed cells: faster with, slower against, unchanged across. They never push a stopped craft.
design.mastery: Reclaim both marked fields completely and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The marked center route disappears behind a stopped craft while neighboring arrows remain.
design.routeDecision: Take the marked run to the central landing, or a shorter unmarked slice near the western platform?

design.captureConsequence: The upper-petal closure leaves the western field broad; the dot-first closure shifts the surviving keeper regions toward the outer petal chain.
design.counterplay: Stage on the central landing for the upper petal, or watch the west keeper before committing to the dot. Each route preserves another safe return if the next read changes.
design.lesson: Five familiar landings form an open spiral, petal and dot rhythm; the finale adds no mandatory mechanic.
design.mastery: Complete both the central-petal and dot-first approaches without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A Lemko-pysanka-informed floral rhythm opens into a central spiral shoulder and four deliberately uneven outer landings.
design.routeDecision: Secure the upper petal from the central spiral shoulder, or connect the western dot first and build an outside return before separating the three keepers?

design.captureConsequence: One keeper retains only the region it occupies at closure.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Reaching reclaimed ground secures a live line; empty regions fill.
design.mastery: Close a cut without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The first enclosure reveals a broad part of the horizon.
design.routeDecision: Cross to the far rail or turn back to the near rail?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Learn to grow a following body and leave room for its next turn. Contact and enclosure both clear targets. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Clear without a lost life, mixing contact and enclosure while keeping the tail clear of your next turn.
design.memorableMoment: Plan a complete circuit through three landings and remove every humanoid.
design.routeDecision: Plan a complete circuit through three landings and remove every humanoid. Starts with capacity 7; grows 1 per catch, up to 12. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: A reclaimed neck removes its speed penalty and changes the value of the next central crossing.
design.counterplay: Compare the keeper positions with both nearby landings. Cross an arrow band at right angles when its direction is unhelpful.
design.lesson: Shortest distance and shortest exposure need not be the same. Across an arrow is ordinary speed, not a sideways push.
design.mastery: Reclaim both central necks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An initially awkward against-arrow route becomes the best ordinary-speed connection after capture.
design.routeDecision: Use the short central neck against the lower arrows or take the longer lateral approach with them?

design.captureConsequence: The shield stays disabled after a life loss. The Sentinel remains a field anchor until its explicit release, which secures the remaining unclaimed picture.
design.counterplay: The chamber walls block movement and never close a cut. Plan the complete return through the opening. Watch both perimeter and frontier patrols when repositioning between attempts.
design.lesson: A shield capture opens a deliberate transition, not an immediate victory. After the vertical attack, close eight fresh trail cells during CORE OPEN or isolate the core.
design.mastery: Release the core in its first exposed opening and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The horizontal shield attack gives way to a vertical core attack after the first relay.
design.routeDecision: Secure an approach to the upper side of the chamber opening, or the lower side, before turning a cut around the enclosed shield?

design.captureConsequence: Securing the middle lets either pilot change chambers through the passage opened by the other.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Securing the middle lets either pilot change chambers through the passage opened by the other.
design.routeDecision: Finish an outer chamber first, or cross the offset passages and secure the middle?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Route a growing body around fixed guard warnings. Keep a wide exit; effects never replace the warning line. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try the numbered target order for bonus points. Any contact or enclosure still clears that target; a missed order never blocks completion.
design.memorableMoment: Plan the outside loop around both warning lanes and choose contact or enclosure for the final guards.
design.routeDecision: Plan the outside loop around both warning lanes and choose contact or enclosure for the final guards. Starts with capacity 13; grows 2 per catch, up to 27. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: One pilot’s enclosure removes a material penalty and opens a full-speed route that the partner can use for the next cut.
design.counterplay: Enclose the lethal crossing before either pilot enters it. Use the west spine for shorter banks, then protect the partner’s longer approach through the newly reclaimed corridor.
design.lesson: The Disruptor creates the keeper window for a material enclosure while the Interceptor protects the exposed partner. Neutralized terrain becomes ordinary shared ground.
design.mastery: Neutralize both material beds with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: One partner opens the marked crossing while the other turns a slow approach into ordinary shared ground.
design.routeDecision: Split the outer bypasses to enclose both material beds, or first link a shared return through the slow approach?

design.captureConsequence: The near band cancels the first commitment quickly. The lower reserve gives later cuts a different escape endpoint while two keepers continue retaining separate field regions.
design.counterplay: Near-band-first keeps exposure short but leaves the remote reserve unclaimed. Lower-reserve-first asks for a longer boundary setup and rewards it with a second permanent return.
design.lesson: A Krolevets-informed band rhythm stays an abstract return network: the pursuer commits visibly, foundations close cuts and walls only screen movement and sensing.
design.mastery: Bank the lower reserve, then close at the near band with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Alternating long and short bands turn the same visible pursuit lock into a choice between immediate safety and a stronger future return.
design.routeDecision: Take the short central band as soon as pursuit commits, or cross the open upper edge and bank the lower reserve before returning through the alternating bands?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: The guard warns before firing; its body and every humanoid target remain one-contact catches. Hunt points are optional.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Use two courtyard entrances to approach the guard and refuge target.
design.routeDecision: Use two courtyard entrances to approach the guard and refuge target.

design.captureConsequence: A shared route turns the final station into a short capture after the earlier targets unlock it.
design.counterplay: Prepare the next return while completing the current objective. Dashed crossed targets are still protected; a warning never requires a synchronized button press.
design.lesson: Team targets open in numbered order and require separate captures. Prepare a return for the next active target.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A shared route turns the final station into a short capture after the earlier targets unlock it.
design.routeDecision: Create a route past all three stations, or concentrate each enclosure around the currently active target?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing either anchor both protects its cell and opens a non-scoring connector. Earned side shortcuts remain vulnerable to warned erosion.
design.counterplay: Do not treat every field contact as a travelling impact. Only the marked carrier sends sparks; the eroder still breaks a live trail immediately. Use the broad center corridor to change your approach.
design.lesson: A territory repair and a carrier closure race are familiar but different decisions. Permanent foundations, opened connectors and captured objective anchors protect the planned return.
design.mastery: Traverse both opened connectors before clearing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: An opened T-shaped return stays intact while a nearby earned edge is reopened.
design.routeDecision: Open the upper protected link first, or invest in the lower anchor while the carrier and eroder occupy different corridors?

design.captureConsequence: Relay corners stay permanent while erosion can restore a marked inner spoke. Trail impacts still disappear when a valid closure secures the trail.
design.counterplay: Enclose the lethal patches and complete the permanent corner circuit first. Repair an inner spoke only when it shortens the next closure; the durable outer route prevents reopened cells from becoming compulsory cleanup.
design.lesson: This optional combination uses only known roles. The protected circuit and earned spokes have different erosion consequences; neither changes the capture contract.
design.mastery: Traverse both opened corners and neutralize both lethal patches before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: Two missing corners become a complete durable circuit around a changing interior.
design.routeDecision: Complete the protected outer circuit through relay corners, or use the shorter marked center while field threats remain on opposite sides?

design.captureConsequence: The route both neutralizes material and changes the frontier leading to the far landing.
design.counterplay: The first island is outside the slow bed; wait there and choose the next approach deliberately.
design.lesson: A slow crossing extends trail exposure while the familiar frontier patrol keeps moving.
design.mastery: Link both landings without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A wide enclosure can remove a slow approach and redirect patrol pressure at once.
design.routeDecision: Bridge the slow center for a large enclosure, or link the landings by a longer clear route?

design.captureConsequence: The first enclosure decides whether the second cut follows a direct lane or an outer detour.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The first enclosure decides whether the second cut follows a direct lane or an outer detour.
design.routeDecision: Remove the slow petal on the left, or turn above the lethal petal for a larger first bank?

design.captureConsequence: The landing becomes a repeatable shortcut without changing which field enemies retain their regions.
design.counterplay: First connect the nearby landing. When an impact appears, close on reclaimed ground before it reaches the craft; a hit at the live endpoint gives no grace.
design.lesson: Only the bolt-shaped carrier sends moving impacts. Ordinary keepers still damage the trail immediately.
design.mastery: Close a cut with an active travelling impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A travelling impact disappears when a short return closes in time.
design.routeDecision: Use the landing as a short return, or pass it for a larger enclosure with more exposed trail?

design.captureConsequence: A line-only link can still shorten both routes while occupied regions remain unclaimed.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower keepers leave different departure windows. Use the intermediate islands to shorten exposure; a wall is never a return.
design.lesson: The return one partner builds is also a launch point for the other.
design.mastery: Connect both intermediate islands to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: An offset chain of four islands becomes one shared route network.
design.routeDecision: Take separate stepping stones, or connect across the centre before spreading out?

design.captureConsequence: An outer enclosure can remove a garden and an approach together, giving the other craft a full-speed return.
design.counterplay: Keep the lethal gardens outside your route until they are reclaimed. Time the central keeper before attempting a shared bridge.
design.lesson: A short route through slow field can keep a trail exposed longer than an outer bypass.
design.mastery: Neutralize every slow and lethal patch with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two dangerous gardens become ordinary shared ground around a contested middle island.
design.routeDecision: Link through a slow approach to reach the middle island, or split the outer routes and clear the gardens first?

design.captureConsequence: One closure can clear a travelling impact and open a permanent connection, but the emitter still retains its field.
design.counterplay: Close before the marked lane fires, then use the new connection while preserving space from an activated roamer.
design.lesson: Combine established relay, lane and impact rules. Opening a link changes return choices, not enemy attack periods.
design.mastery: Open a connector on a cut carrying an active impact and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: An opened link provides a fresh launch point after a narrow closure escapes a known lane attack.
design.routeDecision: Spend the next attack window opening a new escape connection or enclose a smaller region while keeping the roamer dormant?

design.captureConsequence: An outer enclosure removes one material penalty. A central-bank connection instead gives both pilots a short launch toward the opposite garden.
design.counterplay: The Interceptor protects the long central cut while the Disruptor controls the keeper in the chosen garden. Approach opposite bands so one closure changes the other pilot’s route.
design.lesson: Nested and cross-band organization informs the route rhythm only. Walls block movement, while only foundations and completed cuts close a trail.
design.mastery: Connect the central bank, then let each pilot neutralize a different garden without a down.
design.memorableMoment: Two offset cross bands become one shared exchange after the first specialist reaches the nested centre.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize an outer garden for the safer transfer, or expose a longer cut to the nested central bank so both specialists gain the stronger next launch?

design.captureConsequence: The inland landing removes the patrol from the final return decision.
design.counterplay: Watch the next corner and return behind the patrol, or connect an interior refuge before committing to the shore.
design.lesson: Perimeter patrols follow the outside rail. Permanent interior landings give you an alternative return.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The inland landing removes the patrol from the final return decision.
design.routeDecision: Return behind the patrol now, or invest in the inland landing before the next crossing?

design.captureConsequence: A crossbar closure preserves fast access to both sides; a stair-tip closure moves the useful frontier away from the outer rail.
design.counterplay: The crossbar is closest but exposed to the next patrol pass. The stair tip takes longer to reach and offers a quieter east-facing return.
design.lesson: An asymmetric interior return can trade immediate access for a safer later departure while the outer patrol keeps its established route.
design.mastery: Use both the crossbar and stair tip while ignoring the optional timed slow bonus.
design.memorableMoment: A Krychevsky-panel-informed open stair turns one rectangular island into a visible timing choice around the patrolled border.
design.routeDecision: Slip behind the perimeter patrol onto the broad crossbar, or wait longer and descend the open stair to its safer inner tip?

design.captureConsequence: The courtyard and outside field retain their own keeper; neither fills for free.
