design.mastery: Complete an inward cut and an outward cut.
design.memorableMoment: The same return ring changes meaning when approached from the other side.
design.routeDecision: Clear the enclosed courtyard first or build outward from its outer edge?

design.captureConsequence: The side passage remains available when a travelling impact makes the middle route too expensive.
design.counterplay: Keep a second return in reserve; a partner’s new bank can shorten your exposed trail.
design.lesson: An impact follows its original live cut. Close that cut, or use Interceptor Support near the travelling front.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The side passage remains available when a travelling impact makes the middle route too expensive.
design.routeDecision: Develop the quiet side passage first, or take turns crossing the longer southern opening?

design.captureConsequence: A completed chamber contributes earned territory without automatically clearing the other occupied chambers.
design.counterplay: Reposition along the broad cross; the four field keepers cannot leave their starting chambers without a field connection.
design.lesson: Each occupied chamber retains its own field. Permanent cross lanes provide returns but do not earn coverage.
design.mastery: Make captures in three different starting chambers without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same central crossing lets the player choose the order of unequal spatial problems.
design.routeDecision: Start with a small near quadrant, or use the spacious cross to tackle the larger region while its keeper is distant?

design.captureConsequence: The last turn rewards the return network chosen in the opening.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper before leaving safe ground. Both rivals have identical boards and settings; choose a shorter return when the long route is threatened.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Complete the race using both opening plans on separate attempts.
design.memorableMoment: The last turn rewards the return network chosen in the opening.
design.routeDecision: Build a short island ladder, or bank alternating outer strips to race the coverage target?

design.captureConsequence: A short passage connection can make the far band easier to approach without changing patrol domain.
design.counterplay: Use the internal return strips while the outside patrol passes; keep one passage available for the next cut.
design.lesson: Repeated bands do not repeat the same route: their openings alternate sides.
design.mastery: Close a cut through each of the two inner passages.
design.memorableMoment: A left-to-right crossing becomes a right-to-left problem at the next band.
design.routeDecision: Cross at the staggered inner passage, or circle the end of the textile-like band for a larger enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: A side connection changes the nearby patrol frontier, while a shoulder enclosure establishes an exterior return. Open wall sections remain walls and do not create a separate capture rule.
design.counterplay: Leave from the side away from the frontier patrol. Read the inside keeper before the right-side cut, or use the visible shoulder gap to reach the longer outside approach.
design.lesson: Inspect the wall above the starting reclaimed pad. The open stepped shell blocks movement but is not a return surface; only keeper positions decide retained field, and the frontier patrol follows reclaimed edges.
design.mastery: Use both the side opening and northern shoulder approach before clearing without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The short side opening and longer stepped shoulder lead to different useful return surfaces around the same open egg silhouette.
design.routeDecision: Connect through the broad right-side opening and reshape the nearby frontier, or pass around the northern shoulder to establish the exterior left return first?

design.captureConsequence: The sideways cut sacrifices acceleration but leaves a shorter trail under pressure.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The sideways cut sacrifices acceleration but leaves a shorter trail under pressure.
design.routeDecision: Cross the field at right angles, or follow its arrows to the farther landing?

design.captureConsequence: Capture order determines which branch remains a convenient return under pressure.
design.counterplay: Use the broad central branch to switch sides; leave another return available before enlarging the roamer’s domain.
design.lesson: An escape corridor needs a usable departure, not merely a connection to reclaimed cells occupied by a roamer.
design.mastery: Connect both outer platforms and neutralize the marked pocket without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The best next capture opens a way out rather than maximizing immediate area.
design.routeDecision: Build an outside escape to the near platform, or neutralize the marked pocket before joining the far platform?

design.captureConsequence: West-first neutralizes the slow approach for later repairs; east-first shortens the long side and leaves the central island as an emergency reserve.
design.counterplay: Keep the central island available until one eroder commits. The western approach costs speed; the eastern wrap costs exposure but banks a second permanent return.
design.lesson: Örnek-informed grouped geometry separates permanent islands with open wall shoulders; earned links can erode while every authored foundation survives.
design.mastery: Join all three islands, repair one eroded link and finish without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A reopened link changes the route, but the separated island grouping keeps two legible recovery choices on the board.
design.routeDecision: Take the short slowing approach into the western grouped island, or wrap the clear eastern shoulder to establish a reserve before either eroder reaches the next earned link?

design.captureConsequence: The first captured area becomes the return surface for a shorter second cut.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Longer exposed routes can earn more ground, but the keeper chooses which region remains.
design.mastery: Complete the mission in three cuts or fewer.
design.memorableMoment: A cautious first cut changes the best route for the next one.
design.routeDecision: Take the nearby narrow slice now, or travel along the rail for a larger enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: The relay adds a non-scoring permanent return; erosion may restore arrows only on the earned side routes.
design.counterplay: Use the protected connector as a fallback and follow erosion and lane warnings. Neither forces a repair before another route is available.
design.lesson: Combine known arrow, erosion and relay rules: foundations and opened connectors are permanent; earned marked territory can reactivate.
design.mastery: Use the protected connector and reclaim both side currents before clearing without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: The center connector stays dependable while a reopened current visibly changes a side route.
design.routeDecision: Secure the permanent return first or invest in an earned sideways shortcut that erosion may reopen into an arrow field?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralizing either outer thread changes the best route to the middle platform; the remaining occupied field still requires a deliberate closure.
design.counterplay: The long side spines offer many departures. Go above or below the walls, never into the lethal notches; the central keeper preserves the middle until isolated.
design.lesson: A partner can turn a slow approach into a fast shared return before the second cut begins.
design.mastery: Neutralize every material patch and connect the middle platform to the perimeter, with closures from both craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two winding approaches become one short route through the reclaimed middle.
design.routeDecision: Weave around opposite wall tips to bank the middle, or clear one material lane and share that approach?

design.captureConsequence: The first bridge changes return distance while the outer route remains fixed.
design.counterplay: Both landings offer return choices without needing the pickup.
design.lesson: Touch the optional life pickup on reclaimed ground; enclosing it is not collection.
design.mastery: Use both landings before clearing.
design.memorableMoment: A deliberate detour across the landing earns a visible recovery bonus.
design.routeDecision: Use the long landing to wait out a patrol pass, or bridge to the shorter far landing?

design.captureConsequence: A rewarding capture can create both new return ground and a new threat on that ground.
design.counterplay: The first island return wakes the sleeper behind you. Watch its one-second warning, then use either side of the broad platform for your next departure.
design.lesson: A dormant roamer does not retain field. Reclaiming its full body starts a warning, then it moves and threatens reclaimed ground.
design.mastery: Activate the roamer and complete another closure without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Your first thin connection wakes a threat on the very ground you just reclaimed; the broad landing gives room to choose a way out.
design.routeDecision: Wake the sleeper on the short island connection, or build a side return before reclaiming its corridor?

design.captureConsequence: Each capture changes which pilot benefits from the remaining directional field.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: Each capture changes which pilot benefits from the remaining directional field.
design.routeDecision: Open a direct survey return through the arrows, or leave the fast lane for a later long enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: The shield stays disabled after a life loss. The Sentinel remains a field anchor until its explicit release, which secures the remaining unclaimed picture.
design.counterplay: The chamber walls block movement and never close a cut. Plan the complete return through the opening. Watch both perimeter and frontier patrols when repositioning between attempts.
design.lesson: A shield capture opens a deliberate transition, not an immediate victory. After the vertical attack, close eight fresh trail cells during CORE OPEN or isolate the core.
design.mastery: Release the core in its first exposed opening and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The horizontal shield attack gives way to a vertical core attack after the first relay.
design.routeDecision: Secure an approach to the upper side of the chamber opening, or the lower side, before turning a cut around the enclosed shield?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Read elbows, pockets and switchbacks before the body reaches them. The shortest line is not always the easiest turn. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Enter the wide yard only after choosing which side will carry your return.
design.routeDecision: Enter the wide yard only after choosing which side will carry your return. Starts with capacity 5; grows 1 per catch, up to 9. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: The final return follows a path both partners built before the two rover pockets woke.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The final return follows a path both partners built before the two rover pockets woke.
design.routeDecision: Connect the whole dock network first, or take turns enclosing rover pockets while the partner keeps an escape open?

design.captureConsequence: Near-panel play leaves the far crossing exposed; far-panel play creates a useful return beyond the lethal bed before it is neutralized.
design.counterplay: The near panel supports a short cautious cut. The northern shoulder offers a longer setup only after the east keeper and perimeter patrol separate.
design.lesson: Three unequal returns frame the lethal field without turning it into a wall; neutralizing it still requires a valid enemy-seeded enclosure.
design.mastery: Reach the far panel before neutralizing the complete lethal bed.
design.memorableMoment: A Kosiv-ceramics-informed three-panel frame makes the dangerous centre a route-order problem instead of one rectangular detour.
design.routeDecision: Establish the near framed panel before enclosing the lethal bed, or cross the safe northern shoulder and build a longer approach toward the far panel?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Read elbows, pockets and switchbacks before the body reaches them. The shortest line is not always the easiest turn. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Alternate left and right passages; do not reverse into the body trailing behind you.
design.routeDecision: Alternate left and right passages; do not reverse into the body trailing behind you. Starts with capacity 6; grows 1 per catch, up to 10. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: An interior return lets the partner avoid a border segment that is temporarily occupied.
design.counterplay: Watch the next corner and return behind the patrol, or connect an interior refuge before committing to the shore.
design.lesson: Perimeter patrols follow the outside rail. Permanent interior landings give you an alternative return.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a useful return and complete every required target without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: An interior return lets the partner avoid a border segment that is temporarily occupied.
design.routeDecision: Connect the internal watchpost before visiting the perimeter, or return to the outer rail behind its patrol?

design.captureConsequence: The inner closure keeps the frontier near the original elbow; the outer closure creates a farther return behind the lower dogleg and shifts its useful contour.
design.counterplay: Read the frontier from the permanent L. The inner elbow is shorter; the outer shoulder is valuable only when the east keeper is moving away from its exposed line.
design.lesson: Bukovyna-pysanka-informed sectioning adds broad wave and dogleg wall masses while the established moving-frontier rule remains unchanged.
design.mastery: Close once from each shoulder without collecting the optional slow bonus.
design.memorableMoment: A single broad wave-like opening turns the same L-shaped foundation into a quick inside cut or a committed outside wrap.
design.routeDecision: Take the short inner elbow while the moving frontier is leaving it, or wrap the longer outer shoulder for a larger first capture and a different later return?

design.captureConsequence: The chosen enclosure changes the contour around one arm and the next useful return.
design.counterplay: Use the broad L-shaped foundation to change approach; the optional slow pickup is not required.
design.lesson: Practice changing a frontier route before combining it with an outer patrol.
design.mastery: Close from both arms without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A new return draws the frontier patrol around a different side of the L.
design.routeDecision: Extend the short arm to redirect contour pressure, or reach around the long arm for more ground?

design.captureConsequence: The shortcut creates a different final route from the same central landing.
design.counterplay: Choose which new return is most useful before choosing which relay to capture first.
design.lesson: Capture each required relay to open its matching permanent bridge. Choose an order that shortens later cuts.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The shortcut creates a different final route from the same central landing.
design.routeDecision: Buy the upper shortcut with a small relay cut, or claim the western pocket and reach the switch from below?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: These explicitly marked specialists have dangerous facing or burst phases. Read their warning, approach the exposed side, or eliminate them by enclosure.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Wait out the brace warning and intercept its recovery.
design.routeDecision: Wait out the brace warning and intercept its recovery.

design.captureConsequence: Permanent-loop-first preserves fallback departures. Bank-first neutralizes immediate danger and creates a fast route that remains strategically expendable.
design.counterplay: The upper loop resists erosion but crosses the lane warning more often. A bank-first route is shorter after capture, yet its earned return must be repaired or abandoned when marked.
design.lesson: A Polissia woven-curtain record informs separated-band organization only. Walls remain permanent blockers; cooled hazards can still return when earned territory erodes.
design.mastery: Neutralize both banks, connect every foundation and recover from one erosion event.
design.memorableMoment: A warned bank reopens while the separated permanent loop remains available on the opposite side of the wall field.
design.routeDecision: Connect the permanent northern and side landings through the separated upper bands, or neutralize a lethal bank through the lower brackets before erosion can reopen its shortcut?

design.captureConsequence: The prepared approach shortens the final fresh cut when the core enters its open phase.
design.counterplay: Prepare the core approach before the last shield. If the open window closes, wait for the next readable attack cycle.
design.lesson: Capture both shield relays in either order, then release the exposed sentinel core with a fresh cut during its open phase.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The prepared approach shortens the final fresh cut when the core enters its open phase.
design.routeDecision: Capture the near shield first, or establish a core approach before opening either shield?

design.captureConsequence: A bridge between lanes creates a new return and can move the contour across the next intended approach.
design.counterplay: The upper and lower gaps stay wide; wait on a foundation and choose the side away from patrol pressure.
design.lesson: Staggered return lanes reward planning the next departure, not just reaching the nearest reclaimed cell.
design.mastery: Join all three return lanes without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: One diagonal-looking route is executed as clear orthogonal cuts between staggered platforms.
design.routeDecision: Alternate the broad top and bottom connections, or take a slow central link to reshape the frontier sooner?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: Caps follow patrol circuits; hoods seek distant refuges; scarves follow committed switchback routes.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Match a four-corner patrol from either of two island approaches.
design.routeDecision: Match a four-corner patrol from either of two island approaches.

design.captureConsequence: An inner landing shortens a later cut without banking against a wall. Outer returns introduce reclaimed-ground pressure, and two retainers keep each chamber contested until deliberately enclosed.
design.counterplay: The top and bottom baffle ends stay open. Watch both local keepers before crossing; after waking a roamer, turn onto a different return rather than waiting on its new rail. Either partner may travel around the divider to help.
design.lesson: Each chamber offers a short changing return and a longer inner connection; opening one chamber never clears the other occupied field.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers, with each craft closing in its starting chamber and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: A quick outside escape and a protected inner receiver become two different ways to reopen the same depot.
design.routeDecision: Wake the outer return patrols for quick perimeter access, or wrap the inner baffles to establish receiver landings first?

design.captureConsequence: Material neutralization and roamer activation can occur in the same enclosure; both partners must read the changed board.
design.counterplay: Use the side spines to change departure heights. Enclose crosses before entering them and leave space around the courtyard when a roamer wakes.
design.lesson: Removing a terrain hazard does not make every reclaimed route free of enemies.
design.mastery: Activate both roamers and connect the courtyard to the perimeter, with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: A dangerous garden becomes passable just as the tracked bodies make the surrounding ground busy.
design.routeDecision: Neutralize the upper hazard before linking the courtyard, or establish the lower slow-field approach while the partner prepares a different exit?

design.captureConsequence: A capture changes your return options but can create an eligible frontier for erosion.
design.counterplay: Watch the eroder stop and mark a cell. Keep a permanent return within reach instead of chasing every lost cell.
design.lesson: The marked cell warns before reopening. Foundations remain permanent; earned ground can need repair.
design.mastery: Repair an eroded cell with a legal closure without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A small gap reopens beside a landing that stays intact.
design.routeDecision: Use the permanent landing for repeated returns, or bank a larger exposed edge that the eroder can reopen?

design.captureConsequence: Relay order produces different exposure budgets without changing either rival’s board.
design.counterplay: Choose which new return is most useful before choosing which relay to capture first.
design.lesson: Capture each required relay to open its matching permanent bridge. Choose an order that shortens later cuts.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: Relay order produces different exposure budgets without changing either rival’s board.
design.routeDecision: Dispatch the western link first, or take the eastern relay that shortens two future crossings?

design.captureConsequence: Remove every humanoid to finish. Enclosure and contact both count; percentage, catch chains and target order are not additional clear requirements.
design.counterplay: Plan a wide exit before turning. Humanoids flee, round keepers remain dangerous, and a return does not remove a tail unless this mission explicitly sheds segments.
design.lesson: Keep a longer body moving around islands and staggered walls. Build returns without cutting across your own wake. Your body follows your route and grows after every humanoid removed by contact or enclosure. Avoid your own trailing body; the capture line remains a separate rule.
design.mastery: Try consecutive catches within ten seconds for a chain bonus. The main clear has no countdown.
design.memorableMoment: Choose a gap or an outer shore; make the choice before the tail enters the gap.
design.routeDecision: Choose a gap or an outer shore; make the choice before the tail enters the gap. Starts with capacity 9; grows 2 per catch, up to 19. Returns retain the body.

design.captureConsequence: A contact earns 100 Hunt points; a captured target earns 50. Hunt points are separate from territory score.
design.counterplay: Choose a short return before leaving the rail. Hunt points are optional here; capture 30% to finish.
design.lesson: Touching a humanoid removes it immediately. No attack button or power-up is needed. The round keeper remains dangerous.
design.mastery: Remove a runner by touch and complete the ordinary capture goal.
design.memorableMoment: Remove a runner by touch and complete the ordinary capture goal.
design.routeDecision: Touch the nearby runner on your first cut, then return to the rail.

design.captureConsequence: The bridge offers a permanent alternative when the sentinel’s locked lane crosses the direct approach.
design.counterplay: Prepare the core approach before the last shield. If the open window closes, wait for the next readable attack cycle.
design.lesson: Capture both shield relays in either order, then release the exposed sentinel core with a fresh cut during its open phase.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The bridge offers a permanent alternative when the sentinel’s locked lane crosses the direct approach.
design.routeDecision: Open the vault bridge before the shields, or capture a shield en route to the shortcut?

design.captureConsequence: A line-only first cut establishes a permanent return lane for later enclosures.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Two occupied regions can keep their field even though the closing line is reclaimed.
design.mastery: Create and then use a line-only return lane.
design.memorableMoment: The board explains why both occupied sides remain dark.
design.routeDecision: Separate the two keepers first or wait until they share one side?

design.captureConsequence: The two original gates become the same permanent, unscored connectors. Each earns a useful launch beside a different wall opening, so relay order changes the next approach rather than merely collecting two markers.
design.counterplay: Go around the wall above the west landing to enclose its relay. After opening that bridge, the middle platform offers a shorter approach around the eastern lower hook; the outer rail remains a longer alternative.
design.lesson: The open vytynanka-inspired vase forms are walls around capture links. Each relay still opens only its own permanent connector; the shapes do not create new triggers or return surfaces.
design.mastery: Open the eastern connector before the western connector, using its upper opening, and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A relay reached from outside the first open vase turns the middle landing into the inside approach to the second.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the near relay around its open vase shoulder and use the earned middle launch, or reach the eastern trigger around its upper negative-space opening from the boundary first?

design.captureConsequence: Territory capture remains the objective. Touch earns 100 Hunt points; enclosure earns 50 per accepted target.
design.counterplay: Read the ordinary keeper before leaving safe ground. Prefer interception over a long chase.
design.lesson: The guard warns before firing; its body and every humanoid target remain one-contact catches. Hunt points are optional.
design.mastery: Catch every optional target by contact and complete the capture objective without damage.
design.memorableMoment: Let the guard lock its aim before committing to the nearest return.
design.routeDecision: Let the guard lock its aim before committing to the nearest return.

design.captureConsequence: Each braid remains an independent permanent return. Joining one reshapes the moving frontier while preserving the other as a deliberate alternate home.
design.counterplay: West-first offers the shorter exposed drop. East-first uses the central wall rhythm to screen one approach, then turns after the finite lock toward the longer return.
design.lesson: Hutsul diagonal alternation becomes two original stepped return networks. Their offsets create different approach timings without changing pursuit rules.
design.mastery: Connect both stepped returns and close at the second one with an active impact without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A committed pursuer crosses the abandoned centre as the craft closes on the opposite stepped braid.
design.routeDecision: Commit to the nearer west braid before the frontier reaches its shoulder, or feint through the centre and close at the east braid after the pursuer locks the old heading?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a new inner return does not redirect the outer patrol.
design.counterplay: The first island offers an interior return while the patrol stays on the outside rail.
design.lesson: Reclaimed ground closes a cut, but the outer patrol can still hit the craft there.
design.mastery: Complete without touching the outer patrol.
design.memorableMoment: A return inside the board avoids a dangerous stretch of the outer rail.
design.routeDecision: Leave before the outer patrol approaches, or wait for it to pass and return behind it?

design.captureConsequence: A captured outer entrance gives the partner a short return while the middle keeper retains the courtyard.
design.counterplay: Keep a short return available for both pilots. Interceptor Support clears nearby travelling impacts; Disruptor Support slows a keeper. Support is optional.
design.lesson: Close onto foundations or reclaimed ground. Walls stop movement and never close a live trail.
design.mastery: Both pilots bank a cut and use a return opened by their partner, without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: A captured outer entrance gives the partner a short return while the middle keeper retains the courtyard.
design.routeDecision: Meet through the courtyard’s central opening, or secure the outer entrances first?

design.captureConsequence: A successful enclosure turns the dangerous center into a new traversable return surface.
design.counterplay: The first return and broad outside approaches avoid the marked bed entirely.
design.lesson: Framed crosses harm the craft on unclaimed field. Capturing that field neutralizes the hazard.
design.mastery: Neutralize the whole central bed without visiting the far landing first.
design.memorableMoment: The crossed warning disappears from earned ground without changing the underlying map rule.
design.routeDecision: Enclose the marked central bed before crossing, or keep a longer clear path around it?

design.captureConsequence: Near-first play builds a broad western network; far-first play redirects pressure before the centre and west are connected.
design.counterplay: The near rim offers the shortest closure. The lower centre gives a staging return, while the far reversed rim is safest just after its frontier patrol leaves the mouth.
design.lesson: Unequal contour mouths create different timing windows even though every bay follows the same retained-region and frontier rules.
design.mastery: Connect all three contour frames while using both a broad and a narrow mouth.
design.memorableMoment: Three Opishne-bowl-informed interrupted contours read as near rim, lower centre and reversed far rim instead of three repeated boxes.
design.routeDecision: Secure the nearby interrupted rim and its broad landing, or cross the open centre to reach the far reversed rim before its patrol returns?

design.captureConsequence: The central station provides a short return on either side of a locked column.
design.counterplay: Wait on permanent ground during a warning, or take a short return. Capturing a Team emitter disables its future warnings.
design.lesson: A numbered pilot and dashed lane mark the locked warning. Close the original cut before the lane fires.
design.mastery: Both pilots contribute a capture and use the shared return without a knockdown.
design.memorableMoment: The central station provides a short return on either side of a locked column.
design.routeDecision: Join the central station before a column locks, or work the two outer bays independently?

design.captureConsequence: Closure cancels the committed attack. Field-retaining enemies still determine which regions remain unclaimed, and the existing terrain or patrol consequences remain active.
design.counterplay: Use the dogleg to break line of sight, wait through the finite commitment, and cross each occupied chamber toward its nearest genuine return.
design.lesson: Physical walls and reclaimed ground block sensing; the dogleg closes cuts, but a wall alone never becomes a return surface.
design.mastery: Make a closure in both starting chambers and neutralize the lower lethal pocket without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The same stepped structure first screens pursuit and then closes a cut at a different height.
design.routeDecision: Screen the upper route behind the dogleg before a larger enclosure, or clear the lower chamber first and keep the central step as an emergency return?

design.captureConsequence: The final race combines a chosen shield order, a readable attack window and the route built at the start.
design.counterplay: Plan the next return before committing. A bridge, cleared arrow band or captured hazard can simplify your final crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The final race combines a chosen shield order, a readable attack window and the route built at the start.
design.routeDecision: Reclaim the tailwind before opening the final shield, or leave it active for the decisive core approach?

design.captureConsequence: Capturing a relay joins its store to the spine and gives a shorter later departure without mandatory corridor cleanup.
design.counterplay: Use the open side of each store to enclose a trigger instead of tracing every bend of the structure.
design.lesson: A shortcut changes return distance, not the meaning of the surrounding open field. Broad exits remain available before either relay.
design.mastery: Open both shortcuts within two consecutive captures and clear without a life loss.
design.memorableMoment: An apparently winding route becomes a direct permanent connection after one deliberate enclosure.
design.routeDecision: Break the western inward route at the top or the eastern route at the bottom before moving across the central spine?

design.captureConsequence: The central landing creates a short repeatable crossing. The lower landing changes the next launch angle while the emitter and keeper continue retaining occupied field.
design.counterplay: Central-first remains the short close and the lower landing remains the stronger return. A warned freeze window relocates across the three open corridors, but waiting for it can cost the next row-lock cycle.
design.lesson: A Kyiv-area woven-belt record informs only the long narrow cadence. The row lock remains telegraphed, foundations close cuts and band walls never become return ground.
design.mastery: Bank the lower landing, then close at the central landing during an active row warning without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The optional freeze window and the next lane warning overlap on different corridors, making the safe close and the ambitious detour visibly disagree.
design.routeDecision: Close at the compact central landing during the first row warning, or chain that safe close directly into the lower corridor for a stronger second departure?

design.captureConsequence: The tailwind connection becomes a normal-speed final return after capture.
design.counterplay: Read the far landing before departure. Capturing an arrow field removes its speed effect.
design.lesson: Arrows make exposed movement faster with the arrow and slower against it; sideways movement is unchanged. They never push a stopped pilot.
design.mastery: Clear without losing a life after using the chapter mechanic to shorten a return.
design.memorableMoment: The tailwind connection becomes a normal-speed final return after capture.
design.routeDecision: Take the longer tailwind, or cut the short unmarked northern corner?

design.captureConsequence: The route both neutralizes material and changes the frontier leading to the far landing.
design.counterplay: The first island is outside the slow bed; wait there and choose the next approach deliberately.
design.lesson: A slow crossing extends trail exposure while the familiar frontier patrol keeps moving.
design.mastery: Link both landings without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: A wide enclosure can remove a slow approach and redirect patrol pressure at once.
design.routeDecision: Bridge the slow center for a large enclosure, or link the landings by a longer clear route?

design.captureConsequence: One closure can remove a garden and its slow approach, opening a full-speed route that the other craft can use for the next enclosure.
design.counterplay: Assign the Interceptor to the exposed bridge and the Disruptor to the keeper nearest the chosen garden. Enclose lethal terrain instead of crossing it; the resulting reclaimed approach is useful to both craft.
design.lesson: Interceptor Support protects exposed Team lines while Disruptor Support slows the keeper guarding a material enclosure. A completed enclosure neutralizes its terrain for either partner.
design.mastery: Neutralize every slow and lethal patch with a closure from each craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two dangerous gardens become ordinary shared ground around a contested middle island.
design.routeDecision: Link through a slow approach to reach the middle island, or split the outer routes and clear the gardens first?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralized vertical links simplify later travel, but the stationary emitter still retains field and follows the same attack schedule.
design.counterplay: Stage on a broad platform; wait out the lower lane warning without drawing, then choose a return above it or through its recovery.
design.lesson: Arrow speed changes travel time, not attack warnings or enemy speed. Read the full route and the next landing before using a window.
design.mastery: Reclaim the east and west marked links and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: Opposing long lanes stop being asymmetric after they are reclaimed.
design.routeDecision: Use the short alternating vertical links or make a wider unmarked capture during a visible lane-emitter recovery?

design.captureConsequence: A neutralized broad lane becomes a full-speed approach. A middle connection lets the partner exchange lanes and use that approach without repeating the exposed cut.
design.counterplay: The Interceptor covers the longer middle connection while the Disruptor opens a keeper window beside the chosen material lane. Start on different bands to preserve two exits.
design.lesson: Variable-width band organization informs the thread spacing only. The elongated opening is a route decision, not a copied textile motif.
design.mastery: Have each pilot neutralize one broad lane, then exchange sides through the middle opening.
design.memorableMoment: The team turns separate thin and broad threads into one shared crossing with two viable exits.
design.routeDecision: Link a thin separator to the middle opening, or neutralize a broad material lane before the partner exchanges sides?

design.captureConsequence: New links change route length; the keepers still determine which regions fill.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.lesson: Connected islands turn one long exposure into several shorter decisions.
design.mastery: Connect all three islands before the clear.
design.memorableMoment: A chain of small connections makes the broad final enclosure possible.
design.routeDecision: Join successive islands for short returns or bypass one for a larger enclosure?

design.captureConsequence: Neutralizing either outer thread changes the best route to the middle platform; the remaining occupied field still requires a deliberate closure.
design.counterplay: The long side spines offer many departures. Go above or below the walls, never into the lethal notches; the central keeper preserves the middle until isolated.
design.lesson: A partner can turn a slow approach into a fast shared return before the second cut begins.
design.mastery: Neutralize every material patch and connect the middle platform to the perimeter, with closures from both craft and no knockdowns.
design.memorableMoment: Two winding approaches become one short route through the reclaimed middle.
design.routeDecision: Weave around opposite wall tips to bank the middle, or clear one material lane and share that approach?

design.captureConsequence: The bridge leaves a permanent core approach available during the sentinel’s open window.
design.counterplay: Plan the next return before committing. A bridge, cleared arrow band or captured hazard can simplify your final crossing.
design.lesson: Combine the chapter’s visible mechanics. Numbered objectives and coverage are both required; ordinary foundations stay permanent.
design.mastery: Finish every required objective without losing a life, preserving a short final return.
design.memorableMoment: The bridge leaves a permanent core approach available during the sentinel’s open window.
design.routeDecision: Open the bridge before attacking the shield relays, or take a shield on the route to the shortcut?

design.captureConsequence: A reclaimed neck loses its speed modifier. A lateral closure instead establishes ordinary return ground outside the inner bands while both keepers remain active.
design.counterplay: North-first limits exposure but gives the frontier a predictable contour. West-first is longer, uses favourable arrows and preserves both central necks for later cuts.
design.lesson: A museum towel record informs separated-rhombus and outward-branch organization only. Wall gaps define the compass choices without forcing a turn or changing capture rules.
design.mastery: Secure the west arm first, then reclaim both central necks and clear without losing a life.
design.memorableMoment: The apparently decorative branch ends become readable timing gates around the central compass pad.
design.routeDecision: Use the short north neck between the inner rhombus bands, or cross the longer west arm with its arrows before the frontier reaches the central landing?

method.coverage: All registered fixed Solo/Versus authored routes and Team lifecycle routes; Classic base/bundled/archived/optional/external; legacy Team arenas. Company editions and their presentation overrides are not yet inventoried. Imported user content is not classified.
method.gameplayComparison: Standard host physics after the current versioned gameplay-tuning recipe, including Classic class recipes; authored physics is separately hashed. Display/revision identities are removed and entity references consistently renamed. Mode host rules remain separate; equal definitions require design review.
method.geometryComparison: Static placements only; timing, threat behaviour and rules remain in full gameplay comparisons.
limitations: Only non-interlaced RGB8 PNG originals receive full portable pixel decoding. Other accepted PNG variants and JPEG/WebP originals receive exact byte and header checks; null pixel hashes cannot establish pixel or visual uniqueness.
Company-edition missions, presentation overrides and retained artwork revisions remain outside this inventory. The complete shipped-content inventory gate is not yet satisfied.
Perceptual, crop, rotation/reflection and human visual checks remain required before uniqueness approval.
Package artwork counts are not complete download totals; use the generated offline catalogue for dependency closures and full sizes.
Archive policy changes discovery only. Historical readers, original bytes and saved identities remain unchanged.
method.proceduralComparison: Exact renderer command hash at seed0; different seeds do not establish different compositions.
